This differential is historically significant because it helps explain why Japanese American internment was implemented while German Americans were largely not mass-interned — the same racial framework that dehumanized Japan's population in propaganda supported the view that Japanese Americans were inherently suspect regardless of citizenship. Options B, C, and D mischaracterize the propaganda's significance or miss the racial analysis.
items.explanationEs: El encuadre racial diferencial en la propaganda bélica refleja directamente las jerarquías raciales estadounidenses existentes: los japoneses fueron racializados como no blancos y por lo tanto susceptibles a la caricatura racial de maneras que los europeos blancos no lo eran. La distinción entre los 'líderes nazis' y 'el pueblo alemán' preservó la humanidad de los europeos blancos incluso cuando eran enemigos, mientras que generalmente no se hacía tal distinción para los soldados y civiles japoneses. Esta diferencia es históricamente significativa porque ayuda a explicar por qué el internamiento japonés americano se implementó mientras que los alemanes americanos en gran medida no fueron internados masivamente —el mismo marco racial que deshumanizó a la población de Japón en la propaganda apoyó la opinión de que los japoneses americanos eran inherentemente sospechosos independientemente de la ciudadanía—. Las opciones B, C y D tergiversan la importancia de la propaganda o pierden el análisis racial.

items.stem: The sale of war bonds during World War II raised approximately $185 billion from ordinary Americans. Bond drives were promoted through celebrity endorsements, school campaigns, and patriotic events. Analyzing the economic and political functions of war bonds, which of the following best explains their dual role?
items.stemEs: La venta de bonos de guerra durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial recaudó aproximadamente $185 mil millones de los estadounidenses ordinarios. Las campañas de bonos se promovieron a través de endosos de celebridades, campañas escolares y eventos patrióticos. Analizando las funciones económicas y políticas de los bonos de guerra, ¿cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor su doble papel?

choices.text: War bonds were purely a financing mechanism that served no political or morale function — their sole purpose was raising the revenue needed to pay for military equipment and operations without requiring tax increases on ordinary Americans.
choices.textEs: Los bonos de guerra fueron puramente un mecanismo de financiamiento que no tenía ninguna función política —su único propósito fue recaudar los ingresos necesarios para pagar el equipo militar sin aumentar los impuestos.

choices.text: War bonds were purely a morale and propaganda tool — they raised minimal actual war revenue relative to total war costs but successfully created a powerful illusion of broad public participation and shared sacrifice in the war effort.
choices.textEs: Los bonos de guerra fueron puramente una herramienta de moral y propaganda —recaudaron ingresos mínimos de guerra reales pero crearon exitosamente la ilusión de participación pública en el esfuerzo bélico.

choices.text: War bonds primarily benefited wealthy investors who purchased them in large quantities to gain favorable tax treatment, while their actual anti-inflation effect was negligible due to the relatively small individual quantities purchased by ordinary working-class citizens.
choices.textEs: Los bonos de guerra beneficiaron principalmente a los inversores adinerados que los compraron en grandes cantidades por ventajas fiscales, mientras que su efecto antiinflacionario fue mínimo debido a las pequeñas cantidades compradas por los ciudadanos ordinarios.

choices.text: War bonds served dual functions: absorbing civilian purchasing power to reduce inflationary pressure while making ordinary Americans literal financial stakeholders in Allied victory, generating broad participatory investment in the war effort.
choices.textEs: Los bonos de guerra sirvieron funciones económicas y políticas duales simultáneamente: absorbieron el poder adquisitivo civil para reducir la presión inflacionaria mientras hacían a los estadounidenses individuales accionistas financieros literales en la victoria aliada, creando una inversión participativa en el esfuerzo bélico que generó tanto estabilidad económica antiinflacionaria como compromiso ciudadano con el resultado.

items.explanation: War bonds served two distinct but complementary functions: (1) Economic — they absorbed consumer purchasing power that could not be spent on consumer goods (which were being rationed or not produced) and directed it toward government war finance, reducing inflationary pressure. By channeling civilian savings into government bonds rather than consumer spending, bonds helped prevent the wage-price spiral inflation that had characterized WWI. (2) Political — they created citizen investment in the war effort in the most literal sense, making individual Americans financially stakeholders in Allied victory. A bond-holder had personal financial interest in the war being won and the bonds being repayable. This created participatory legitimacy for the war. Options A, B, and C capture only one dimension each.
items.explanationEs: Los bonos de guerra sirvieron dos funciones distintas pero complementarias: (1) Económica —absorbieron el poder adquisitivo del consumidor que no podía gastarse en bienes de consumo (que estaban siendo racionados o no producidos) y lo dirigieron hacia las finanzas gubernamentales de guerra, reduciendo la presión inflacionaria. Al canalizar los ahorros civiles hacia los bonos gubernamentales en lugar del gasto del consumidor, los bonos ayudaron a prevenir la inflación de espiral salario-precio que había caracterizado la Primera Guerra Mundial—. (2) Política —crearon inversión ciudadana en el esfuerzo bélico en el sentido más literal, haciendo a los estadounidenses individuales accionistas financieros en la victoria aliada. Un tenedor de bonos tenía interés financiero personal en que se ganara la guerra y los bonos pudieran ser reembolsados. Esto creó legitimidad participativa para la guerra—. Las opciones A, B y C capturan solo una dimensión cada una.

items.stem: The wartime home front experience — rationing, bond drives, victory gardens, factory conversion, and propaganda — has been characterized by some historians as a period of genuine democratic participation in the war effort and by others as a period of government-managed consent. Analyzing the available evidence, which of the following best evaluates these competing characterizations?
items.stemEs: La experiencia del frente doméstico en tiempo de guerra —racionamiento, campañas de bonos, jardines de la victoria, conversión de fábricas y propaganda— ha sido caracterizada por algunos historiadores como un período de participación democrática genuina en el esfuerzo bélico y por otros como un período de consentimiento gestionado por el gobierno. Analizando la evidencia disponible, ¿cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor estas caracterizaciones en competencia?

choices.text: The home front was a period of purely genuine democratic participation — Americans freely and voluntarily chose to support the war effort, and government propaganda functioned as a neutral, transparent information source rather than a consent-manufacturing tool.
choices.textEs: El frente doméstico fue puramente un período de participación democrática genuina —los estadounidenses libre y voluntariamente eligieron apoyar la guerra, y la propaganda gubernamental fue una fuente de información neutral en lugar de una herramienta de fabricación de consentimiento.

choices.text: The home front combined genuine voluntary participation — Americans had real patriotic motivations — with systematic narrative management by the OWI, which censored uncomfortable information and shaped consent beyond neutral information provision, creating a reality reducible to neither pure democracy nor pure manipulation.
choices.textEs: La experiencia del frente doméstico combinó una participación voluntaria genuina —los estadounidenses tenían motivaciones patrióticas reales— con la gestión sistemática del gobierno de las narrativas a través de la OWI, que censuró información incómoda y moldeó el consentimiento de maneras que iban más allá de la provisión neutral de información, creando una realidad compleja que no puede reducirse a pura democracia o pura manipulación.

choices.text: The home front experience was purely manufactured consent — all apparent citizen participation was systematically orchestrated by government propaganda agencies, and ordinary Americans had no genuine agency in expressing wartime patriotism outside of what the state sanctioned.
choices.textEs: El frente doméstico fue puramente consentimiento fabricado —toda la aparente participación ciudadana fue orquestada por agencias de propaganda gubernamentales, y los estadounidenses ordinarios no tuvieron ninguna agencia genuina para expresar el patriotismo en tiempo de guerra.

choices.text: The question of genuine participation versus managed consent is historically difficult to answer because assessing ordinary citizens' internal motivations requires reading private sources critically against the grain of official propaganda records produced by the OWI itself.
choices.textEs: La pregunta sobre la participación genuina versus el consentimiento gestionado es históricamente inanswerable porque no hay evidencia suficiente sobre las motivaciones internas de los ciudadanos ordinarios para determinar si sus acciones fueron voluntarias o coaccionadas.

items.explanation: The home front experience was neither purely voluntary democratic participation nor purely manufactured consent — it was both simultaneously. Americans did voluntarily sacrifice, plant victory gardens, buy bonds, and work in war industries with genuine patriotic motivation. At the same time, government propaganda agencies (OWI — Office of War Information) carefully managed narratives, censored information, and shaped public opinion in ways that went beyond informing to engineering consent. The absence of the full picture of racial conflict, labor disputes, and civilian costs in home front messaging demonstrates the managed nature of the narrative. A DOK 3 evaluation holds both dimensions — genuine participation and managed consent — in productive tension. Options A, C, and D commit to one interpretation and exclude the other.
items.explanationEs: La experiencia del frente doméstico no fue puramente participación democrática voluntaria ni puramente consentimiento fabricado —fue ambas simultáneamente—. Los estadounidenses sí se sacrificaron voluntariamente, plantaron jardines de la victoria, compraron bonos y trabajaron en las industrias de guerra con motivación patriótica genuina. Al mismo tiempo, las agencias de propaganda del gobierno (OWI —Oficina de Información de Guerra) gestionaron cuidadosamente las narrativas, censuraron información y dieron forma a la opinión pública de maneras que iban más allá de informar para diseñar el consentimiento. La ausencia de la imagen completa del conflicto racial, las disputas laborales y los costos civiles en el mensaje del frente doméstico demuestra la naturaleza gestionada de la narrativa. Una evaluación de DOK 3 mantiene ambas dimensiones —participación genuina y consentimiento gestionado— en tensión productiva. Las opciones A, C y D se comprometen con una interpretación y excluyen la otra.

items.stem: The Office of War Information (OWI) managed information and propaganda during World War II, including censorship of newspaper stories, control of film content, and shaping of news coverage. Analyze the tension between the OWI's function and the First Amendment values of a democracy at war.
items.stemEs: La Oficina de Información de Guerra (OWI) gestionó la información y la propaganda durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial, incluida la censura de artículos periodísticos, el control del contenido cinematográfico y la configuración de la cobertura noticiosa. Analiza la tensión entre la función de la OWI y los valores de la Primera Enmienda de una democracia en guerra.

choices.text: The OWI's censorship was completely incompatible with First Amendment values, and its operation demonstrated that the United States was a military dictatorship rather than a functioning democracy during the war.
choices.textEs: La censura de la OWI fue completamente incompatible con los valores de la Primera Enmienda, y su operación demostró que los Estados Unidos era una dictadura militar en lugar de una democracia funcional durante la guerra.

choices.text: The OWI's operations were fully consistent with First Amendment values because wartime security interests always outweigh press freedom, making any government information management during declared wars constitutionally permissible.
choices.textEs: Las operaciones de la OWI fueron plenamente coherentes con los valores de la Primera Enmienda porque los intereses de seguridad en tiempo de guerra siempre superan a la libertad de prensa, haciendo que cualquier gestión gubernamental de la información durante las guerras declaradas sea constitucionalmente permisible.

choices.text: The OWI created genuine constitutional tension: its voluntary cooperation model preserved some press freedom while systematically shaping information — showing the democratic dilemma of balancing security management against the public accountability that democratic legitimacy requires.
choices.textEs: La OWI creó una tensión constitucional genuina: su modelo de cooperación principalmente voluntaria preservó algo de libertad de prensa mientras que daba forma sistemáticamente a la información pública —ilustrando el dilema democrático irreducible de equilibrar la gestión de información de seguridad con la rendición de cuentas pública informada que requiere la legitimidad democrática.

choices.text: The OWI's censorship had no effect on public opinion because Americans had access to uncensored foreign news sources throughout the war, making government information management irrelevant to how citizens understood the conflict.
choices.textEs: La censura de la OWI no tuvo ningún efecto en la opinión pública porque los estadounidenses tenían acceso a fuentes de noticias extranjeras sin censurar durante toda la guerra, haciendo que la gestión gubernamental de la información fuera irrelevante para cómo los ciudadanos entendían el conflicto.

items.explanation: The OWI's operation creates a genuine constitutional and democratic tension: wartime security and morale management require some information control, but a democracy's legitimacy rests on an informed public capable of holding government accountable. The OWI primarily used voluntary cooperation (asking publishers and studios to censor themselves) rather than legal compulsion, which preserved a degree of press freedom while achieving management goals. However, the OWI did suppress information about racial strife, labor conflicts, and civilian war costs that the public arguably had a democratic right to know. This represents a middle ground between the extreme of total information control and total press freedom — a tension inherent to all democracies facing existential threats. Options A, B, and D resolve the tension artificially.
items.explanationEs: La operación de la OWI crea una tensión constitucional y democrática genuina: la seguridad en tiempo de guerra y la gestión moral requieren algún control de la información, pero la legitimidad de una democracia descansa en un público informado capaz de hacer responsable al gobierno. La OWI utilizó principalmente la cooperación voluntaria (pidiendo a editores y estudios que se censuraran a sí mismos) en lugar de la compulsión legal, lo que preservó un grado de libertad de prensa mientras lograba los objetivos de gestión. Sin embargo, la OWI suprimió información sobre conflictos raciales, conflictos laborales y costos civiles de guerra que el público podría haber tenido un derecho democrático a conocer. Esto representa un término medio entre el extremo del control total de la información y la libertad total de prensa —una tensión inherente a todas las democracias que enfrentan amenazas existenciales—. Las opciones A, B y D resuelven la tensión artificialmente.

items.stem: The wartime economic mobilization transformed the American economy: unemployment fell from approximately 14% in 1940 to under 2% by 1943, and GDP grew by over 40% during the war years. Analyzing this economic transformation, which of the following best evaluates its long-term consequences for American economic policy debates?
items.stemEs: La movilización económica en tiempo de guerra transformó la economía estadounidense: el desempleo cayó de aproximadamente el 14% en 1940 a menos del 2% para 1943, y el PIB creció más del 40% durante los años de guerra. Analizando esta transformación económica, ¿cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor sus consecuencias a largo plazo para los debates de política económica estadounidense?

choices.text: The wartime economic data appeared to empirically validate Keynesian economics by demonstrating that massive government spending could eliminate unemployment and generate rapid growth — making WWII mobilization a persistent reference point in post-war debates about fiscal policy and government's role in managing economic cycles.
choices.textEs: Los datos económicos de tiempo de guerra parecieron validar empíricamente la economía keynesiana al demostrar que el gasto gubernamental masivo podía eliminar el desempleo y generar un crecimiento rápido —convirtiendo la movilización de la Segunda Guerra Mundial en un punto de referencia persistente en los debates de posguerra sobre la política fiscal y el papel del gobierno en la gestión de los ciclos económicos.

choices.text: The wartime economic success demonstrated that the free market could achieve full employment without government intervention, as private defense contractors — rather than government spending — were the primary driver of wartime economic growth.
choices.textEs: El éxito económico en tiempo de guerra demostró que el mercado libre podía lograr el pleno empleo sin intervención gubernamental, ya que los contratistas de defensa privados —en lugar del gasto gubernamental— fueron el principal impulsor del crecimiento económico bélico.

choices.text: The wartime economic transformation had no implications for post-war economic policy debates because politicians and economists universally agreed that wartime mobilization economics could not be applied to peacetime conditions.
choices.textEs: La transformación económica bélica no tuvo implicaciones para los debates de política económica de posguerra porque los políticos y economistas coincidieron universalmente en que la economía de la movilización bélica no podía aplicarse a las condiciones de tiempos de paz.

choices.text: The wartime economic data primarily demonstrated that military spending is counterproductive to long-term economic growth because it diverts resources from consumer goods production that would have generated more sustainable prosperity.
choices.textEs: Los datos económicos bélicos demostraron principalmente que el gasto militar es contraproducente para el crecimiento económico a largo plazo porque desvía recursos de la producción de bienes de consumo que habrían generado una prosperidad más sostenible.

items.explanation: The wartime economic data had profound implications for economic policy debates: it appeared to demonstrate empirically that government spending at scale could end mass unemployment and produce rapid economic growth — appearing to validate Keynesian economics in ways that peacetime New Deal spending had been unable to definitively demonstrate (partly because New Deal spending, while significant, was not at the scale of wartime mobilization). This became a key reference point for post-war economic policy debates: Keynesians pointed to WWII as proof that fiscal stimulus works; critics argued that wartime spending was uniquely motivated by external necessity that could not be replicated in peacetime. The empirical record of WWII economic transformation thus became a recurring reference in American macroeconomic policy debates. Options B, C, and D mischaracterize the long-term policy implications.
items.explanationEs: Los datos económicos de tiempo de guerra tuvieron profundas implicaciones para los debates de política económica: parecía demostrar empíricamente que el gasto gubernamental a escala podía acabar con el desempleo masivo y producir un rápido crecimiento económico —aparentemente validando la economía keynesiana de maneras que el gasto del New Deal en tiempos de paz había sido incapaz de demostrar definitivamente (en parte porque el gasto del New Deal, aunque significativo, no era a la escala de la movilización bélica)—. Esto se convirtió en un punto de referencia clave para los debates de política económica de posguerra: los keynesianos señalaron a la Segunda Guerra Mundial como prueba de que el estímulo fiscal funciona; los críticos argumentaron que el gasto bélico estaba motivado de manera única por la necesidad externa que no podía replicarse en tiempos de paz. El registro empírico de la transformación económica de la Segunda Guerra Mundial se convirtió así en una referencia recurrente en los debates de política macroeconómica estadounidense. Las opciones B, C y D tergiversan las implicaciones de política a largo plazo.

items.stem: During World War II, the federal government's power expanded dramatically — through the War Production Board, the Office of Price Administration, rationing programs, and the Manhattan Project. Analyzing the long-term institutional consequences of this wartime expansion of federal power, which of the following best explains its significance for American governance?
items.stemEs: Durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial, el poder del gobierno federal se expandió dramáticamente —a través de la Junta de Producción de Guerra, la Oficina de Administración de Precios, los programas de racionamiento y el Proyecto Manhattan—. Analizando las consecuencias institucionales a largo plazo de esta expansión bélica del poder federal, ¿cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor su importancia para el gobierno estadounidense?

choices.text: Wartime federal expansion was completely reversed after 1945, and the federal government returned to its pre-New Deal size and role, demonstrating that American democratic institutions successfully resist permanent expansion of executive and federal power.
choices.textEs: La expansión federal bélica fue completamente revertida después de 1945, y el gobierno federal regresó a su tamaño y papel previo al New Deal, demostrando que las instituciones democráticas estadounidenses resisten exitosamente la expansión permanente del poder ejecutivo y federal.

choices.text: The wartime expansion of federal power was temporary and had no institutional legacy, as all wartime agencies were immediately abolished and their functions returned to state governments or private markets as soon as combat operations ended.
choices.textEs: La expansión bélica del poder federal fue temporal y no tuvo ningún legado institucional, ya que todas las agencias bélicas fueron inmediatamente abolidas y sus funciones devueltas a los gobiernos estatales o los mercados privados tan pronto como terminaron las operaciones de combate.

choices.text: The wartime expansion reduced federal power over the long term because the massive wartime debt forced post-war governments to cut domestic programs that had been the primary source of federal authority.
choices.textEs: La expansión bélica redujo el poder federal a largo plazo porque la masiva deuda bélica obligó a los gobiernos de posguerra a recortar los programas domésticos que habían sido la fuente principal de la autoridad federal.

choices.text: Wartime federal expansion demonstrated a 'ratchet effect' — emergency powers did not fully contract after the emergency ended, establishing institutional precedents, bureaucratic capacities, and political expectations that persistently elevated the federal government's role in the economy and national security into the post-war era.
choices.textEs: La expansión federal bélica demostró un 'efecto trinquete' —los poderes de emergencia no se contrajeron completamente después de que terminó la emergencia, estableciendo precedentes institucionales, capacidades burocráticas y expectativas políticas que elevaron persistentemente el papel del gobierno federal en la economía y la seguridad nacional en la era de posguerra.

items.explanation: The wartime federal expansion had a 'ratchet effect' documented by political scientists: emergency expansions of federal power typically do not fully contract to pre-emergency levels after the emergency ends. The precedents set during WWII — federal management of industrial production, price controls, research funding (the model that became the National Science Foundation and NIH), and nuclear weapons development — established institutional templates and political expectations for federal capacity that persisted into the post-war era. The Cold War then provided a second justification for maintaining elevated federal defense and research capacities. This ratchet pattern helps explain the long-term trajectory of American government expansion from WWII onward. Options A, B, and C are either empirically incorrect or miss the long-term institutional dynamics.
items.explanationEs: La expansión federal bélica tuvo un 'efecto trinquete' documentado por los politólogos: las expansiones de emergencia del poder federal típicamente no se contraen completamente a los niveles pre-emergencia después de que termina la emergencia. Los precedentes establecidos durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial —gestión federal de la producción industrial, controles de precios, financiamiento de investigación (el modelo que se convirtió en la Fundación Nacional de Ciencias y los NIH) y desarrollo de armas nucleares— establecieron plantillas institucionales y expectativas políticas de capacidad federal que persistieron en la era de posguerra. La Guerra Fría luego proporcionó una segunda justificación para mantener capacidades federales de defensa e investigación elevadas. Este patrón de trinquete ayuda a explicar la trayectoria a largo plazo de la expansión del gobierno estadounidense desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial en adelante. Las opciones A, B y C son empíricamente incorrectas o pierden las dinámicas institucionales a largo plazo.

items.stem: At the Yalta Conference in February 1945, FDR agreed to grant the Soviet Union territorial concessions in Asia in exchange for Stalin's promise to enter the war against Japan after Germany's defeat. Which of the following best explains the strategic reasoning behind this agreement?
items.stemEs: En la Conferencia de Yalta en febrero de 1945, FDR acordó otorgar concesiones territoriales a la Unión Soviética en Asia a cambio de la promesa de Stalin de entrar en la guerra contra Japón después de la derrota de Alemania. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor el razonamiento estratégico detrás de este acuerdo?

choices.text: FDR was unaware of Soviet expansionist ambitions and trusted Stalin's word without strategic calculation.
choices.textEs: FDR desconocía las ambiciones expansionistas soviéticas y confiaba en la palabra de Stalin sin ningún cálculo estratégico.

choices.text: U.S. planners feared the enormous cost of invading Japan and believed Soviet entry would reduce American casualties by forcing Japan to fight on two fronts.
choices.textEs: Los planificadores estadounidenses temían el enorme costo de invadir Japón y creían que la entrada soviética reduciría las bajas americanas al obligar a Japón a combatir en dos frentes.

choices.text: FDR sought to reward the Soviet Union for its sacrifices on the Eastern Front by giving it access to warm-water ports in Asia.
choices.textEs: FDR buscaba recompensar a la Unión Soviética por sus sacrificios en el Frente Oriental dándole acceso a puertos de aguas cálidas en Asia.

choices.text: American military leaders had already confirmed that the atomic bomb would end the war quickly, so the Soviet concessions were purely diplomatic gestures.
choices.textEs: Los líderes militares estadounidenses ya habían confirmado que la bomba atómica terminaría la guerra rápidamente, por lo que las concesiones soviéticas fueron puramente gestos diplomáticos.

items.explanation: U.S. military planners estimated that an invasion of the Japanese home islands could cost hundreds of thousands of American casualties. Soviet entry into the Pacific war would force Japan to fight on two fronts, potentially shortening the conflict and reducing American losses. This strategic calculus — not naivety or deference — drove FDR's willingness to offer territorial concessions. The atomic bomb's success was not yet certain at the time of Yalta (February 1945), so planners could not rely on it as an alternative. This item requires students to reconstruct the decision-making logic under wartime uncertainty rather than simply recall what was agreed.
items.explanationEs: Los planificadores militares estadounidenses estimaban que una invasión de las islas principales de Japón podría costar cientos de miles de bajas americanas. La entrada soviética en la guerra del Pacífico obligaría a Japón a combatir en dos frentes, lo que potencialmente acortaría el conflicto y reduciría las pérdidas estadounidenses. Este cálculo estratégico —no la ingenuidad ni la deferencia— fue lo que impulsó la disposición de FDR a ofrecer concesiones territoriales. El éxito de la bomba atómica aún no era seguro en el momento de Yalta (febrero de 1945), por lo que los planificadores no podían depender de ella como alternativa.

items.stem: The Yalta Conference (February 1945) produced agreements on the post-war occupation of Germany, the formation of the United Nations, and free elections in Eastern Europe. By the time of the Potsdam Conference (July–August 1945), relations among the Allied powers had noticeably deteriorated. Which combination of factors most directly caused this deterioration?
items.stemEs: La Conferencia de Yalta (febrero de 1945) produjo acuerdos sobre la ocupación de Alemania de posguerra, la formación de las Naciones Unidas y elecciones libres en Europa del Este. Para el momento de la Conferencia de Potsdam (julio–agosto de 1945), las relaciones entre las potencias aliadas habían empeorado notablemente. ¿Qué combinación de factores causó más directamente este deterioro?

choices.text: The Soviet Union's decision to withdraw its troops from Germany before Potsdam signaled its abandonment of Allied cooperation.
choices.textEs: La decisión de la Unión Soviética de retirar sus tropas de Alemania antes de Potsdam señaló su abandono de la cooperación aliada.

choices.text: Churchill's replacement by Clement Attlee during the conference weakened Western unity and emboldened Stalin to break prior agreements.
choices.textEs: El reemplazo de Churchill por Clement Attlee durante la conferencia debilitó la unidad occidental y envalentonó a Stalin para romper acuerdos previos.

choices.text: FDR's death removed a conciliatory Western leader, and Soviet violations of Yalta's free-election promises in Eastern Europe heightened mutual distrust.
choices.textEs: La muerte de FDR eliminó a un líder occidental conciliador, y las violaciones soviéticas de las promesas de elecciones libres de Yalta en Europa del Este aumentaron la desconfianza mutua.

choices.text: The United States' refusal to share reparations from Germany with the Soviet Union provoked Stalin into breaking all Yalta commitments.
choices.textEs: La negativa de Estados Unidos a compartir las reparaciones de Alemania con la Unión Soviética provocó que Stalin rompiera todos los compromisos de Yalta.

items.explanation: Between Yalta and Potsdam, two pivotal changes occurred: FDR died (April 1945), removing a leader with an established relationship with Stalin and a conciliatory style, and the Soviets installed communist-dominated governments in Poland and Romania rather than holding the free elections promised at Yalta. These two factors — leadership change and Soviet non-compliance — directly strained Allied relations. Truman arrived at Potsdam deeply suspicious of Soviet intentions. The atomic bomb test (July 16, 1945) also shifted Truman's diplomatic posture, but the ideological friction predated it. Students must synthesize multiple causes rather than identify a single event.
items.explanationEs: Entre Yalta y Potsdam ocurrieron dos cambios fundamentales: FDR murió (abril de 1945), eliminando a un líder con una relación establecida con Stalin y un estilo conciliador, y los soviéticos instalaron gobiernos dominados por comunistas en Polonia y Rumanía en lugar de celebrar las elecciones libres prometidas en Yalta. Estos dos factores —el cambio de liderazgo y el incumplimiento soviético— tensaron directamente las relaciones aliadas. Truman llegó a Potsdam profundamente desconfiado de las intenciones soviéticas.

items.stem: Critics of the Yalta agreements have argued that FDR 'sold out' Eastern Europe to Stalin by legitimizing Soviet dominance over Poland and neighboring countries. Defenders argue that the agreements were the best achievable given military realities. Which evidence most effectively supports the defenders' position?
items.stemEs: Los críticos de los acuerdos de Yalta han argumentado que FDR 'traicionó' a Europa del Este al legitimar la dominación soviética sobre Polonia y los países vecinos. Los defensores argumentan que los acuerdos fueron los mejores posibles dadas las realidades militares. ¿Qué evidencia apoya más efectivamente la posición de los defensores?

choices.text: Soviet forces already occupied most of Eastern Europe by February 1945, leaving FDR with little military leverage to demand different terms.
choices.textEs: Las fuerzas soviéticas ya ocupaban la mayor parte de Europa del Este en febrero de 1945, lo que dejó a FDR con poca palanca militar para exigir condiciones diferentes.

choices.text: FDR secretly agreed to give Stalin permanent control of Poland in exchange for Soviet support at the United Nations.
choices.textEs: FDR acordó en secreto darle a Stalin el control permanente de Polonia a cambio del apoyo soviético en las Naciones Unidas.

choices.text: The United States had no strategic interest in Eastern European independence and viewed Soviet control as acceptable.
choices.textEs: Estados Unidos no tenía ningún interés estratégico en la independencia de Europa del Este y consideraba aceptable el control soviético.

choices.text: Churchill independently negotiated the 'percentages agreement' that gave the Soviets Eastern Europe without FDR's knowledge.
choices.textEs: Churchill negoció de forma independiente el 'acuerdo de porcentajes' que le dio a los soviéticos Europa del Este sin el conocimiento de FDR.

items.explanation: The most powerful rebuttal to the 'sellout' argument is that the Red Army already physically occupied Eastern Europe at the time of Yalta. FDR had no military leverage to remove Soviet forces from Poland or Romania short of starting a new war. The Yalta agreements on free elections were the best diplomatic language FDR could extract; the subsequent Soviet violation of those promises is what created the Cold War reality. Students must evaluate competing historical interpretations using evidence rather than simply siding with one view.
items.explanationEs: El argumento más poderoso contra la tesis de la 'traición' es que el Ejército Rojo ya ocupaba físicamente Europa del Este en el momento de Yalta. FDR no tenía palanca militar para sacar las fuerzas soviéticas de Polonia o Rumanía sin iniciar una nueva guerra. Los acuerdos de Yalta sobre elecciones libres fueron el mejor lenguaje diplomático que FDR pudo obtener; la posterior violación soviética de esas promesas fue lo que creó la realidad de la Guerra Fría.

items.stem: At the Potsdam Conference, President Truman informed Stalin that the United States had 'a new weapon of unusual destructive force.' Stalin's reaction appeared calm and indifferent. Historians have since argued that Stalin already knew about the Manhattan Project through Soviet espionage. Which of the following best explains why Truman's disclosure strategy backfired diplomatically?
items.stemEs: En la Conferencia de Potsdam, el presidente Truman informó a Stalin que Estados Unidos tenía 'una nueva arma de fuerza destructiva inusual'. La reacción de Stalin pareció tranquila e indiferente. Los historiadores han argumentado desde entonces que Stalin ya sabía del Proyecto Manhattan a través del espionaje soviético. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor por qué la estrategia de divulgación de Truman fracasó diplomáticamente?

choices.text: Truman's disclosure was too specific, giving Stalin enough technical information to accelerate Soviet bomb production immediately.
choices.textEs: La revelación de Truman fue demasiado específica, dándole a Stalin suficiente información técnica para acelerar inmediatamente la producción soviética de la bomba.

choices.text: Stalin was genuinely unaware of the weapon and simply chose not to react publicly so as not to show weakness before his advisers.
choices.textEs: Stalin genuinamente desconocía el arma y simplemente eligió no reaccionar públicamente para no mostrar debilidad ante sus asesores.

choices.text: Truman's vague phrasing confused Stalin, who interpreted the disclosure as a reference to conventional bombs rather than a nuclear device.
choices.textEs: La redacción vaga de Truman confundió a Stalin, quien interpretó la revelación como una referencia a bombas convencionales en lugar de un dispositivo nuclear.

choices.text: Because Stalin already knew through espionage, Truman gained no leverage; instead, the disclosure signaled U.S. intent to use nuclear monopoly diplomatically, deepening Soviet suspicion.
choices.textEs: Dado que Stalin ya lo sabía a través del espionaje, Truman no obtuvo ninguna ventaja; en cambio, la revelación señaló la intención de EE.UU. de usar el monopolio nuclear diplomáticamente, profundizando la desconfianza soviética.

items.explanation: Truman's vague disclosure was designed to signal American strength and perhaps accelerate Japanese surrender negotiations without fully informing Stalin. However, because Stalin already knew through espionage (Klaus Fuchs, etc.), his calm response denied Truman any psychological leverage. Moreover, the disclosure confirmed for Stalin that the U.S. would not share the technology, accelerating Soviet bomb development. Rather than intimidating Stalin, the disclosure revealed American intent to use nuclear monopoly as a diplomatic tool — which deepened Soviet suspicion and accelerated the arms race. This item requires students to evaluate cause and consequence through multiple perspectives.
items.explanationEs: La vaga revelación de Truman estaba diseñada para señalar la fortaleza estadounidense y tal vez acelerar las negociaciones de rendición japonesa sin informar completamente a Stalin. Sin embargo, dado que Stalin ya lo sabía a través del espionaje (Klaus Fuchs, etc.), su reacción tranquila privó a Truman de cualquier ventaja psicológica. Además, la revelación confirmó para Stalin que EE.UU. no compartiría la tecnología, acelerando el desarrollo soviético de la bomba. En lugar de intimidar a Stalin, la revelación reveló la intención estadounidense de usar el monopolio nuclear como herramienta diplomática, lo que profundizó la desconfianza soviética.

items.stem: Both the Yalta Conference and the Potsdam Conference dealt with the question of German reparations. At Yalta, the Soviets proposed $20 billion in reparations (half going to the USSR). At Potsdam, the Western Allies agreed that each occupying power would extract reparations from its own zone. Which of the following best explains why the Western Allies shifted their position between the two conferences?
items.stemEs: Tanto la Conferencia de Yalta como la de Potsdam trataron la cuestión de las reparaciones alemanas. En Yalta, los soviéticos propusieron $20 mil millones en reparaciones (la mitad para la URSS). En Potsdam, los aliados occidentales acordaron que cada potencia ocupante extraería reparaciones de su propia zona. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor por qué los aliados occidentales cambiaron su posición entre las dos conferencias?

choices.text: Western Allies feared that a fixed reparations total would bankrupt Germany and prevent it from paying war debts owed to the United States from World War I.
choices.textEs: Los aliados occidentales temían que un total fijo de reparaciones llevaría a Alemania a la bancarrota e impediría que pagara las deudas de guerra adeudadas a Estados Unidos desde la Primera Guerra Mundial.

choices.text: Western Allies feared that heavy Soviet reparations extraction across all zones would cripple German economic recovery, destabilize Western occupation zones, and push desperate Germans toward communism.
choices.textEs: Los aliados occidentales temían que la extracción soviética de reparaciones en todas las zonas paralizaría la recuperación económica alemana, desestabilizaría las zonas de ocupación occidentales y empujaría a los alemanes desesperados hacia el comunismo.

choices.text: The Western Allies shifted because they believed Germany had been fully de-industrialized and had no remaining industrial capacity from which to extract reparations.
choices.textEs: Los aliados occidentales cambiaron de posición porque creían que Alemania había sido completamente desindustrializada y no tenía capacidad industrial restante de la cual extraer reparaciones.

choices.text: The shift was driven primarily by British pressure, since Churchill objected to paying any reparations to the Soviet Union given its territorial gains in Eastern Europe.
choices.textEs: El cambio fue impulsado principalmente por la presión británica, ya que Churchill se oponía a pagar cualquier reparación a la Unión Soviética dado sus ganancias territoriales en Europa del Este.

items.explanation: The Western Allies — particularly the U.S. — remembered the lesson of the Versailles reparations, which had contributed to German economic collapse and the rise of Hitler. By Potsdam, they also worried that Soviet extraction of reparations from all zones would strip Germany of the economic capacity needed for reconstruction and political stability, potentially pushing a desperate German population toward communism. Limiting reparations to each power's own zone protected Western zones from Soviet extraction while allowing Germany to rebuild. This requires students to connect historical precedent (Versailles), contemporary politics, and strategic interests.
items.explanationEs: Los aliados occidentales —especialmente EE.UU.— recordaban la lección de las reparaciones de Versalles, que habían contribuido al colapso económico alemán y al ascenso de Hitler. Para Potsdam, también les preocupaba que la extracción soviética de reparaciones de todas las zonas despojaría a Alemania de la capacidad económica necesaria para la reconstrucción y la estabilidad política, empujando potencialmente a una población alemana desesperada hacia el comunismo.

items.stem: The Potsdam Declaration (July 26, 1945) warned Japan of 'prompt and utter destruction' if it did not surrender unconditionally. Japan's military government initially rejected the ultimatum. Which of the following best explains why Japanese military leaders chose to continue fighting despite the warning?
items.stemEs: La Declaración de Potsdam (26 de julio de 1945) advirtió a Japón de una 'destrucción rápida y total' si no se rendía incondicionalmente. El gobierno militar de Japón rechazó inicialmente el ultimátum. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor por qué los líderes militares japoneses eligieron continuar luchando a pesar de la advertencia?

choices.text: Japanese leaders believed the United States was bluffing and lacked the military capacity to launch another major offensive after the costly battles of Iwo Jima and Okinawa.
choices.textEs: Los líderes japoneses creían que Estados Unidos estaba fanfarroneando y carecía de capacidad militar para lanzar otra ofensiva importante después de las costosas batallas de Iwo Jima y Okinawa.

choices.text: Japan was awaiting a Soviet mediation offer that would allow it to negotiate a peace settlement that avoided any American occupation.
choices.textEs: Japón esperaba una oferta de mediación soviética que le permitiera negociar un acuerdo de paz que evitara cualquier ocupación americana.

choices.text: Japanese military leaders feared that unconditional surrender would destroy the emperor system, which they viewed as a non-negotiable element of Japanese sovereignty and cultural identity.
choices.textEs: Los líderes militares japoneses temían que la rendición incondicional destruyera el sistema imperial, que consideraban un elemento innegociable de la soberanía e identidad cultural japonesa.

choices.text: Japan's military leaders were unaware of the severity of American industrial and air power after years of propaganda that had minimized Allied capabilities.
choices.textEs: Los líderes militares de Japón desconocían la gravedad del poder industrial y aéreo estadounidense después de años de propaganda que había minimizado las capacidades aliadas.

items.explanation: Japanese military leaders (and much of the civilian leadership) viewed unconditional surrender as a national humiliation and feared it would mean the abolition of the emperor system (kokutai), which they considered sacred and non-negotiable. Many also believed that demonstrated resistance — through the prospect of enormous American casualties in an invasion — could force a negotiated peace that preserved the emperor. The declaration did not specify the emperor's fate, which was precisely the ambiguity Japanese leaders found most alarming. Students must reason about how cultural and political factors shape military decisions rather than applying a purely rational-cost calculus.
items.explanationEs: Los líderes militares japoneses (y gran parte del liderazgo civil) consideraban la rendición incondicional como una humillación nacional y temían que significara la abolición del sistema imperial (kokutai), que consideraban sagrado e innegociable. Muchos también creían que la resistencia demostrada —a través de la perspectiva de enormes bajas americanas en una invasión— podría forzar una paz negociada que preservara al emperador. La declaración no especificaba el destino del emperador, que era precisamente la ambigüedad que más alarmaba a los líderes japoneses.

items.stem: A historian argues: 'The Yalta Conference did not cause the Cold War — it was the subsequent Soviet violation of Yalta's free-election promises that transformed a wartime alliance into a Cold War rivalry.' Which piece of evidence would most directly support this argument?
items.stemEs: Un historiador sostiene: 'La Conferencia de Yalta no causó la Guerra Fría — fueron las posteriores violaciones soviéticas de las promesas de elecciones libres de Yalta las que transformaron una alianza de guerra en una rivalidad de la Guerra Fría'. ¿Qué evidencia apoyaría más directamente este argumento?

choices.text: Despite Yalta's promise of free elections, the Soviet Union installed a communist-dominated government in Poland in 1945 and suppressed the London exile government.
choices.textEs: A pesar de la promesa de Yalta de elecciones libres, la Unión Soviética instaló un gobierno dominado por comunistas en Polonia en 1945 y suprimió el gobierno en el exilio de Londres.

choices.text: FDR's declining health at Yalta made him unable to negotiate firm enforcement mechanisms for the free-election agreements.
choices.textEs: El deterioro de la salud de FDR en Yalta le impidió negociar mecanismos de aplicación firmes para los acuerdos de elecciones libres.

choices.text: Churchill had already agreed in the 1944 'percentages agreement' to give the Soviets dominance over Romania and Bulgaria in exchange for British dominance in Greece.
choices.textEs: Churchill ya había acordado en el 'acuerdo de porcentajes' de 1944 darle a los soviéticos dominio sobre Rumanía y Bulgaria a cambio del dominio británico en Grecia.

choices.text: Truman's decision to end Lend-Lease aid to the Soviet Union immediately after Germany's defeat signaled American hostility before any Soviet violations occurred.
choices.textEs: La decisión de Truman de terminar la ayuda Lend-Lease a la Unión Soviética inmediatamente después de la derrota de Alemania señaló la hostilidad americana antes de que ocurriera cualquier violación soviética.

items.explanation: The historian's argument rests on a causal chain: Yalta produced written agreements for free elections in Eastern Europe → the Soviets agreed to them in good faith (or at least formally) → Soviet actions in Poland and Romania after Yalta violated those agreements → these violations, not the agreements themselves, created the Cold War divide. Evidence of Soviet-installed governments in Poland replacing the London exile government directly proves the violation-of-agreements step in this causal chain. Students must identify which evidence most specifically supports the causal claim being made, not just a related fact.
items.explanationEs: El argumento del historiador descansa en una cadena causal: Yalta produjo acuerdos escritos para elecciones libres en Europa del Este → los soviéticos acordaron con buena fe (o al menos formalmente) → las acciones soviéticas en Polonia y Rumanía después de Yalta violaron esos acuerdos → estas violaciones, no los acuerdos en sí, crearon la división de la Guerra Fría. La evidencia de los gobiernos instalados por los soviéticos en Polonia reemplazando al gobierno en el exilio de Londres prueba directamente el paso de violación de acuerdos en esta cadena causal.

items.stem: At Potsdam, the Allied powers agreed to divide Germany into four occupation zones (American, British, French, Soviet). This decision had long-term consequences not fully anticipated at the time. Which of the following best explains how the occupation zone structure contributed to the permanent division of Germany?
items.stemEs: En Potsdam, las potencias aliadas acordaron dividir Alemania en cuatro zonas de ocupación (americana, británica, francesa, soviética). Esta decisión tuvo consecuencias a largo plazo que no fueron completamente anticipadas en ese momento. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor cómo la estructura de zonas de ocupación contribuyó a la división permanente de Alemania?

choices.text: The zone boundaries were drawn along pre-existing German state (Länder) borders, and states in the Soviet zone voted to join the communist bloc through democratic referendums.
choices.textEs: Los límites de las zonas se trazaron a lo largo de las fronteras preexistentes de los estados alemanes (Länder), y los estados de la zona soviética votaron en referéndums democráticos para unirse al bloque comunista.

choices.text: The Potsdam Agreement explicitly stated that Germany should eventually be divided into two permanent nations, with the Western zones forming one state and the Soviet zone another.
choices.textEs: El Acuerdo de Potsdam establecía explícitamente que Alemania eventualmente debería dividirse en dos naciones permanentes, con las zonas occidentales formando un estado y la zona soviética otro.

choices.text: German political leaders in each zone independently chose to align with their occupying power's ideology, making unification politically impossible from the start.
choices.textEs: Los líderes políticos alemanes en cada zona eligieron independientemente alinearse con la ideología de su potencia ocupante, haciendo la unificación políticamente imposible desde el principio.

choices.text: The ideologically incompatible Western and Soviet systems embedded in separate zones made economic and political integration impossible, ultimately producing two separate German states by 1949.
choices.textEs: Los sistemas occidental y soviético ideológicamente incompatibles incorporados en zonas separadas hicieron imposible la integración económica y política, produciendo en última instancia dos estados alemanes separados para 1949.

items.explanation: The occupation zone structure created administratively separate territories governed by powers with fundamentally incompatible economic and political systems. When the Western Allies introduced a new currency (Deutschmark) in their zones in 1948, the Soviets responded with the Berlin Blockade. The Western zones merged into West Germany (FRG) in 1949 while the Soviet zone became East Germany (GDR). The administrative separation embedded at Potsdam, combined with ideological incompatibility, made reunification impossible until 1990. Students must trace a multi-step causal chain from a decision to its unintended long-term consequence.
items.explanationEs: La estructura de zonas de ocupación creó territorios administrativamente separados gobernados por potencias con sistemas económicos y políticos fundamentalmente incompatibles. Cuando los aliados occidentales introdujeron una nueva moneda (el marco alemán) en sus zonas en 1948, los soviéticos respondieron con el Bloqueo de Berlín. Las zonas occidentales se fusionaron en Alemania Occidental (RFA) en 1949, mientras que la zona soviética se convirtió en Alemania Oriental (RDA). La separación administrativa incorporada en Potsdam, combinada con la incompatibilidad ideológica, hizo imposible la reunificación hasta 1990.

items.stem: Compare the outcomes of the Yalta Conference (February 1945) with those of the Potsdam Conference (July–August 1945). Which conclusion is best supported by examining both conferences together?
items.stemEs: Compare los resultados de la Conferencia de Yalta (febrero de 1945) con los de la Conferencia de Potsdam (julio–agosto de 1945). ¿Qué conclusión está mejor respaldada al examinar ambas conferencias juntas?

choices.text: Both conferences produced durable agreements that successfully maintained Allied unity and prevented the Cold War from developing until the late 1940s.
choices.textEs: Ambas conferencias produjeron acuerdos duraderos que mantuvieron exitosamente la unidad aliada y evitaron que la Guerra Fría se desarrollara hasta finales de la década de 1940.

choices.text: The shift from Yalta to Potsdam demonstrates that American policy became more isolationist as victory neared and leaders focused on domestic reconstruction.
choices.textEs: El cambio de Yalta a Potsdam demuestra que la política estadounidense se volvió más aislacionista a medida que se acercaba la victoria y los líderes se centraban en la reconstrucción interna.

choices.text: The two conferences together trace the transition from wartime alliance to Cold War rivalry, as Soviet violations of Yalta commitments and leadership changes eroded Allied cooperation by the time of Potsdam.
choices.textEs: Las dos conferencias en conjunto trazan la transición de la alianza de guerra a la rivalidad de la Guerra Fría, ya que las violaciones soviéticas de los compromisos de Yalta y los cambios de liderazgo erosionaron la cooperación aliada para el momento de Potsdam.

choices.text: Potsdam reversed most of the Yalta agreements, demonstrating that Truman rejected FDR's entire foreign policy framework in favor of a confrontational stance toward all former allies.
choices.textEs: Potsdam revirtió la mayoría de los acuerdos de Yalta, demostrando que Truman rechazó todo el marco de política exterior de FDR a favor de una postura confrontacional hacia todos los ex aliados.

items.explanation: Taken together, Yalta and Potsdam reveal a trajectory: at Yalta, the Allies still maintained a cooperative framework, producing agreements on elections, the UN, and German occupation. By Potsdam, the cooperative language had largely collapsed — disputes over German reparations, Polish government recognition, and the Soviet sphere were visible. The shift was driven by FDR's death, Soviet violations of Yalta commitments, the successful atomic test, and Truman's harder line. Together, the two conferences represent the transition from wartime alliance to Cold War confrontation. This comparative analysis item requires synthesis across events rather than recall of either conference in isolation.
items.explanationEs: Tomadas en conjunto, Yalta y Potsdam revelan una trayectoria: en Yalta, los aliados todavía mantenían un marco cooperativo, produciendo acuerdos sobre elecciones, la ONU y la ocupación alemana. Para Potsdam, el lenguaje cooperativo había colapsado en gran medida — eran visibles las disputas sobre las reparaciones alemanas, el reconocimiento del gobierno polaco y la esfera soviética. El cambio fue impulsado por la muerte de FDR, las violaciones soviéticas de los compromisos de Yalta, la exitosa prueba atómica y la línea más dura de Truman. Juntas, las dos conferencias representan la transición de la alianza de guerra a la confrontación de la Guerra Fría.

items.stem: Executive Order 9066 led most directly to —

choices.text: The integration of the U.S. armed forces
The lend-lease program with Allied nations
The forced relocation and internment of Japanese Americans
The desegregation of public schools

items.explanation: Executive Order 9066 (February 19, 1942) authorized the Secretary of War to designate military areas from which 'any or all persons' could be excluded — leading directly to the forced relocation and incarceration of approximately 120,000 persons of Japanese descent (about two-thirds U.S. citizens). Distractor A describes EO 9981 (1948); B describes the Lend-Lease Act (1941); D describes Brown v. Board (1954).
items.explanationEs: La Orden Ejecutiva 9066 (19 de febrero de 1942) autorizó al Secretario de Guerra a designar zonas militares de las cuales 'cualquier persona' podría ser excluida, conduciendo directamente al traslado forzoso y encarcelamiento de aproximadamente 120,000 personas de ascendencia japonesa (cerca de dos tercios ciudadanos estadounidenses). El distractor A describe la EO 9981 (1948); B describe la Ley de Préstamo y Arriendo (1941); D describe Brown v. Board (1954).

items.stem: Executive Order 8802 was issued primarily in response to —

choices.text: A federal court ruling on workplace discrimination
Pressure from civil rights leaders, including A. Philip Randolph's threatened March on Washington
Congressional passage of a national civil rights act
A Supreme Court decision overturning Plessy v. Ferguson

items.explanation: Executive Order 8802 (June 25, 1941) banned discrimination in defense industries and was issued by FDR in direct response to A. Philip Randolph's threatened March on Washington Movement. Distractor A describes a judicial process not involved here; C describes the much later 1964 Civil Rights Act; D describes Brown v. Board (1954).
items.explanationEs: La Orden Ejecutiva 8802 (25 de junio de 1941) prohibió la discriminación en las industrias de defensa y fue emitida por FDR en respuesta directa a la amenaza del Movimiento de la Marcha sobre Washington de A. Philip Randolph. El distractor A describe un proceso judicial no involucrado; C describe la Ley de Derechos Civiles de 1964; D describe Brown v. Board (1954).

items.stem: Hull's vision in this excerpt anticipated the founding of which postwar institution?

choices.text: The United Nations
The Warsaw Pact
The North Atlantic Treaty Organization
The European Union

items.explanation: Secretary of State Cordell Hull's wartime planning for postwar collective security led directly to the 1945 founding of the United Nations (Charter signed June 26, 1945, in San Francisco; entered into force October 24, 1945). Distractor B (Warsaw Pact, 1955) and C (NATO, 1949) are Cold-War alliances; D (EU) is a 1990s economic union.
items.explanationEs: La planificación del Secretario de Estado Cordell Hull para la seguridad colectiva de posguerra condujo directamente a la fundación de las Naciones Unidas en 1945 (Carta firmada el 26 de junio de 1945 en San Francisco; entrada en vigor el 24 de octubre de 1945). El distractor B (Pacto de Varsovia, 1955) y C (OTAN, 1949) son alianzas de la Guerra Fría; D (UE) es una unión económica de los años 1990.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The decision to use atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki remains the most contested decision in American military history. Those who support it argue it saved hundreds of thousands of lives by preventing a land invasion. Those who oppose it argue it was the mass murder of civilians and set a precedent for nuclear terror." — Historian Gar Alperovitz, The Decision to Use the Atomic Bomb, 1995

Which of the following best evaluates the strongest counterargument to the 'lives saved' justification for using atomic bombs on Japan?

choices.text: The atomic bombs failed to destroy Japan's military infrastructure, making them ineffective as weapons of war.
Germany had already surrendered without atomic weapons, proving that Japan could have been defeated through conventional bombing alone.
The Soviet Union's entry into the Pacific war would have forced Japan to surrender without using atomic weapons.
Deliberately killing hundreds of thousands of civilians violates the principle of distinguishing combatants from non-combatants, regardless of the strategic benefit achieved.

items.explanation: The strongest counterargument to the 'lives saved' justification is the deliberate targeting of civilian populations — Hiroshima and Nagasaki were primarily civilian cities, not military installations. Critics argue that deliberately killing hundreds of thousands of civilians, including children, to achieve a military objective violates the principle of distinguishing between combatants and non-combatants that underlies the laws of war. Additionally, some historians argue Japan was already seeking surrender through Soviet mediation, making the bombs unnecessary. Option A is incorrect because this is a tactical criticism, not the strongest moral counterargument. Option B is incorrect because Germany's surrender preceded the bombs and doesn't address Japan's situation. Option C is incorrect because Soviet entry into the Pacific war is a separate consideration, not the primary moral counterargument.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Grand Alliance that won the war was built on military necessity. The alliance that must build the peace requires something deeper — shared values and institutions that can survive the end of the common threat." — Secretary of State George Marshall, Harvard Commencement Address, June 5, 1947

Analyze how Marshall's observation about WWII alliances informed the postwar order. Which of the following best evaluates how the Allied coalition's wartime experience shaped postwar institution-building?

choices.text: The success of the wartime alliance proved that military necessity alone was sufficient to sustain a stable postwar international order.

The wartime alliance's fragility inspired the creation of postwar institutions — NATO, the UN, the Marshall Plan — designed to bind nations through shared values and economic interdependence rather than just common threats.
Marshall concluded that temporary emergency coalitions were the most effective form of international organization and should replace permanent alliances.
The wartime alliance's collapse proved that international cooperation was impossible and that each nation should pursue its own security independently.

items.explanation: Marshall's observation reflects the lesson drawn from WWII's wartime alliance: military necessity can hold together ideologically incompatible partners (the U.S., Britain, and USSR), but it cannot sustain peace. The postwar Western alliance was therefore built on shared institutions and values — NATO (collective security among democracies), the UN, the World Bank, the IMF, and the Marshall Plan — rather than mere strategic interest. These institutions were designed to create binding ties between nations that would outlast any specific threat. Option A is incorrect because Marshall recognized that military alliances alone were insufficient. Option C is incorrect because Marshall specifically called for more than emergency coalitions — he wanted lasting institutions. Option D is incorrect because Marshall was not suggesting returning to isolationism.

items.stem:
Read the excerpt below.

"The Lend-Lease Act allows us to send arms to Britain without technically selling them — we are lending tools to a neighbor whose house is on fire. If the neighbor's house burns down, our own house is next." — President Franklin D. Roosevelt, Press Conference, December 17, 1940

Analyze the legal and political strategy Roosevelt used with the Lend-Lease program. Which of the following best evaluates how Lend-Lease allowed Roosevelt to support Britain while maintaining the appearance of American neutrality?

choices.text: Lend-Lease was a clear violation of the Neutrality Acts that Roosevelt implemented illegally without congressional approval.
Roosevelt was fully transparent that Lend-Lease was a step toward entering the war and used it to prepare the public for eventual military involvement.
Lend-Lease used creative legal framing to provide substantial military aid to Britain while formally complying with neutrality laws and making the policy politically palatable to war-weary Americans.
Lend-Lease was a secret program that Roosevelt implemented without congressional knowledge to avoid public opposition.

items.explanation: Lend-Lease was a political masterstroke that allowed Roosevelt to provide crucial military aid to Britain while working around the legal constraints of the Neutrality Acts and public opposition to entering the war. By framing it as 'lending' rather than selling, Roosevelt avoided the cash-and-carry restrictions and the optics of openly supporting a belligerent. His 'garden hose' analogy made the policy seem reasonable and neighborly. In reality, Lend-Lease was an act of undeclared economic war against Germany. The strategy reflects Roosevelt's skill at managing public opinion and legal constraints while pursuing his strategic goals. Option A is incorrect because Lend-Lease did technically comply with the law — that was the entire point. Option B is incorrect because Roosevelt was explicit about wanting to help Britain. Option D is incorrect because Lend-Lease was not secret — it was publicly debated and passed by Congress.

items.stem:
Use the poster to answer the question.

This 1943 poster by J. Howard Miller, produced for the Westinghouse War Production Coordinating Committee, shows a woman wearing a red polka-dot bandana and work clothes, flexing her bicep. Above her arm, bold text reads 'We Can Do It!' The woman's confident expression and work attire were intended to convey strength and capability. The poster was displayed in Westinghouse factories during World War II.

(Poster by J. Howard Miller, 1943. National Archives and Records Administration.)

To what extent did the wartime changes in women's employment — represented by images like this poster — produce lasting effects on women's roles in American society after World War II ended?

choices.text: Wartime employment created immediate and permanent equality for women in all sectors of the economy after 1945
Wartime changes were partially reversed after 1945, but the experience helped challenge gender expectations and laid groundwork for later feminist movements
Wartime employment had no lasting effects because women willingly returned to domestic life and the experience had no influence on later social movements
Women's workforce participation declined steadily after 1945 and did not recover until the twenty-first century

items.explanation: The effects of WWII on women's employment were significant but mixed. In the short term, many women were laid off or pressured to return to domestic roles after 1945, as returning veterans reclaimed industrial jobs. However, the wartime experience demonstrated women's capacity for industrial work, challenged gender expectations, and helped lay cultural groundwork for the feminist movements of the 1960s and 1970s. Women's labor force participation did gradually increase in subsequent decades. Choice A overstates the immediate permanence of wartime gains. Choice C understates the significance entirely. Choice D is factually incorrect about the direction of long-term trends.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This 1942 photograph from the National Archives shows members of the Mochida family wearing identification tags as they await forced evacuation from their home.

(Photograph, 1942. National Archives, NARA 537505.)

How does the internment of Japanese Americans depicted in this photograph illustrate the tension between national security and civil liberties during wartime?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo ilustra el internamiento la tensión entre la seguridad nacional y las libertades civiles en tiempos de guerra?

choices.text: The Supreme Court immediately ruled internment unconstitutional, forcing the president to release all detainees
Japanese Americans voluntarily accepted relocation because they wanted to prove their patriotism
The internment had no lasting significance because all Japanese Americans were compensated fairly at the time
The government denied due process rights to over 120,000 people based on ethnicity, an action later formally acknowledged as a historic injustice

items.explanation: Japanese American internment demonstrates how wartime fear and racial prejudice led the government to violate constitutional rights without due process, later acknowledged as a grave injustice through the Civil Liberties Act of 1988.
items.explanationEs: El internamiento demuestra cómo el miedo en tiempos de guerra llevó al gobierno a violar los derechos constitucionales.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows Buchenwald survivors after liberation, April 1945.

(Photograph, April 1945. National Archives.)

What lessons did the international community draw from the Holocaust, and how were those lessons institutionalized in the postwar period?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué lecciones sacó la comunidad internacional del Holocausto y cómo se institucionalizaron?

choices.text: The Holocaust had no lasting influence on international law or human rights policy
Nations agreed to prevent future genocide but created no specific legal mechanisms to enforce this commitment
The international response was limited to punishing Nazi leaders and did not establish broader principles

The Holocaust spurred the development of international humanitarian law, the concept of crimes against humanity, the Genocide Convention, and a global commitment — though imperfectly realized — to 'never again' permit systematic state-sponsored atrocities

items.explanation: The Holocaust fundamentally shaped the postwar international order: the Nuremberg Principles established individual criminal responsibility for atrocities; the UN Genocide Convention (1948) defined and criminalized genocide; the Universal Declaration of Human Rights established a global rights framework. However, subsequent genocides in Cambodia, Rwanda, and Bosnia revealed the gap between the 'never again' commitment and enforcement.
items.explanationEs: El Holocausto dio forma al orden internacional de posguerra mediante el derecho humanitario, la Convención del Genocidio y los marcos de derechos humanos.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows Tuskegee Airmen, 1945.

(U.S. Air Force photograph, 1945. Public Domain.)

Analyze the connection between African American military service in World War II and the postwar Civil Rights Movement.
items.stemEs: Analice la conexión entre el servicio militar afroamericano en la Segunda Guerra Mundial y el Movimiento por los Derechos Civiles.

choices.text: Military service had no connection to the Civil Rights Movement because veterans did not participate in activism
African American veterans were satisfied with conditions after the war and did not seek further change
Veterans who fought for democracy abroad returned unwilling to accept racial inequality at home, providing leadership and moral authority for the Civil Rights Movement
The military was fully integrated during the war, so there was no remaining inequality to address

items.explanation: The 'Double V' campaign — victory over fascism abroad and racism at home — connected wartime service to civil rights. African American veterans returned with combat experience, organizational skills, and a refusal to accept second-class citizenship. Veterans like Medgar Evers became civil rights leaders. The contradiction of fighting for freedom while facing Jim Crow at home gave the movement powerful moral authority.
items.explanationEs: Los veteranos que lucharon por la democracia en el extranjero regresaron sin disposición a aceptar la desigualdad racial, proporcionando liderazgo al Movimiento por los Derechos Civiles.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows veterans attending college under the GI Bill.

(Photograph, c. 1947. Public Domain.)

Evaluate the extent to which the GI Bill's benefits were distributed equitably across racial groups in postwar America.
items.stemEs: Evalúe en qué medida los beneficios del GI Bill se distribuyeron equitativamente entre grupos raciales.

choices.text: The GI Bill was perfectly equitable and provided identical benefits and opportunities to all veterans regardless of race

While the law was race-neutral on paper, discriminatory implementation — including segregated universities, redlined neighborhoods, and biased VA offices — meant Black veterans received significantly fewer benefits
The GI Bill explicitly excluded all African American veterans from receiving any benefits
Racial discrimination in GI Bill implementation was limited to Southern states and did not exist in the North

items.explanation: The GI Bill's text was race-neutral, but its implementation was deeply unequal. Black veterans were denied admission to most white colleges; VA home loans were refused in redlined neighborhoods; and local VA offices in the South steered Black veterans away from benefits. The result was that the GI Bill massively expanded the white middle class while largely excluding Black veterans, widening the racial wealth gap for generations.
items.explanationEs: Aunque la ley era neutral en raza, la implementación discriminatoria significó que los veteranos negros recibieron significativamente menos beneficios.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows Interstate Highway construction.

(Photograph, c. 1956. Public Domain.)

Analyze the unintended social consequences of the Interstate Highway System shown in this photograph.
items.stemEs: Analice las consecuencias sociales no intencionadas del Sistema de Autopistas Interestatales.

choices.text: Highway construction displaced urban communities — disproportionately African American neighborhoods — accelerated white flight to suburbs, and contributed to the decline of inner cities and public transit
The highways benefited all communities equally and had no negative social effects
The Interstate System strengthened urban neighborhoods by bringing more traffic and commerce to city centers
Highway construction only affected rural areas and had no impact on cities

items.explanation: While the Interstate System generated enormous economic benefits, it also devastated urban communities. Highway planners routinely routed freeways through Black neighborhoods, destroying homes and businesses. Combined with FHA-backed suburban housing (often with racially restrictive covenants), the highways accelerated white flight, hollowed out urban tax bases, undermined public transit, and deepened racial and economic segregation.
items.explanationEs: La construcción de autopistas desplazó comunidades urbanas, aceleró la fuga blanca a los suburbios y profundizó la segregación racial.

items.stem:
Use the image to answer the question.

This WWII war bonds poster, c. 1943.

(U.S. Government poster, c. 1943. Public Domain.)

Evaluate how government propaganda and economic mobilization during World War II transformed the American economy and society.
items.stemEs: Evalúe cómo la propaganda gubernamental y la movilización económica transformaron la economía y sociedad estadounidenses.

choices.text: The wartime economy had no lasting effects because the economy returned to its pre-war state immediately after 1945
Government propaganda was ineffective and most Americans opposed the war effort
Economic mobilization only affected the military sector and had no impact on civilian life

Wartime mobilization ended the Depression, created full employment, expanded women's roles in the workforce, and established a model for government-directed economic planning that influenced postwar policy

items.explanation: WWII's economic mobilization was transformative: unemployment dropped from 14% to under 2%; GDP doubled; women entered the workforce in unprecedented numbers (6 million); the military-industrial complex was born; the GI Bill reshaped postwar society. Government-directed planning demonstrated that federal spending could drive full employment, influencing Keynesian economic policy for decades.
items.explanationEs: La movilización bélica terminó la Depresión, creó pleno empleo, expandió los roles de las mujeres e influyó en la política económica de posguerra.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows women welders in a WWII shipyard.

(Photograph, c. 1943. Public Domain.)

To what extent did women's wartime contributions lead to lasting changes in women's roles in American society?
items.stemEs: ¿En qué medida las contribuciones bélicas de las mujeres condujeron a cambios duraderos en los roles femeninos?

choices.text: While most women were pushed back into domestic roles after the war, their demonstrated capabilities during WWII challenged gender norms and laid groundwork for the women's movement of the 1960s-1970s
Women's wartime employment led to immediate and permanent equality in the workplace
Women's wartime contributions had no lasting impact because they were completely forgotten after 1945
Women voluntarily left industrial jobs because they preferred domestic life

items.explanation: The impact was complex: after the war, social pressure and returning veterans pushed most women out of industrial jobs, and the 1950s emphasized domesticity. However, women's wartime experience created a lasting contradiction — they had proven their capabilities but were told to return to the kitchen. This tension fueled Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique (1963) and the broader women's liberation movement.
items.explanationEs: La experiencia de guerra creó una contradicción duradera que alimentó el movimiento de liberación femenina de los años 1960-1970.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from Admiral Chester Nimitz's communiqué on the Battle of Midway, June 1942 (Department of the Navy press release, 1942; National Archives, public domain):
