items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from the Helsinki Accords (Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe, Final Act), August 1, 1975 — a multilateral international agreement available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School:

"The participating States will respect each other's sovereign equality and individuality as well as all the rights inherent in and encompassed by its sovereignty... They will also respect each other's right freely to choose and develop its political, social, economic and cultural systems as well as its right to determine its laws and regulations... The participating States regard as inviolable all one another's frontiers as well as the frontiers of all States in Europe."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of détente and arms control (US.68), write a CER response that evaluates the Helsinki Accords as both an achievement and a limitation of détente. Your response must analyze what the Accords accomplished in practical terms, identify the tensions embedded in the human rights provisions versus the recognition of Soviet-controlled borders, and assess how the Helsinki process ultimately contributed to the erosion of Soviet control in Eastern Europe (US.70).
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento de los Acuerdos de Helsinki (Conferencia sobre Seguridad y Cooperación en Europa, Acta Final), 1 de agosto de 1975 — un acuerdo internacional multilateral disponible a través del Proyecto Avalon de la Escuela de Derecho de Yale:

"Los Estados participantes respetarán la igualdad soberana e individualidad mutua, así como todos los derechos inherentes a ella y comprendidos en ella... También respetarán el derecho de cada uno a elegir y desarrollar libremente sus sistemas políticos, sociales, económicos y culturales..."

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la distensión y el control de armamentos (US.68), escribe una respuesta CER que evalúe los Acuerdos de Helsinki tanto como un logro como una limitación de la distensión.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — The Helsinki Accords were a double-edged instrument of détente: they gave the Soviet Union what it wanted (recognition of post-WWII European borders) while embedding human rights commitments that Eastern European dissidents and Western critics used to delegitimize Soviet control, ultimately becoming a long-term catalyst for the collapse of communist regimes in 1989–1991. EVIDENCE — (1) The Accords' three 'baskets': security (border recognition), economics, and human rights — the Soviets prioritized Basket I while underestimating Basket III; (2) the emergence of Helsinki Watch Groups in the USSR, Poland, Czechoslovakia, and Hungary (1976–1977) — civil society organizations that monitored Soviet compliance and publicized violations; (3) Solidarity movement in Poland (1980–1981) citing Helsinki human rights provisions; (4) Charter 77 in Czechoslovakia as a direct Helsinki-inspired document; (5) the SALT I and SALT II context as the arms control backbone of détente; (6) Reagan's abandonment of détente framing but continuation of arms control negotiations eventually producing INF Treaty (1987). REASONING — The student should reason that the Helsinki Accords reveal the fundamental asymmetry of détente: the Soviet Union pursued détente primarily to achieve strategic parity recognition and economic access, while the West's inclusion of human rights language created a legitimacy framework that empowered internal opposition. This made the Accords a long-term strategic victory for the West even though they appeared to legitimize Soviet dominance of Eastern Europe in the short term.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.68, US.70 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Claim identifies the double-edged nature of Helsinki. Evidence includes at least three specific details: the three baskets structure, Helsinki Watch Groups, Solidarity, Charter 77, or SALT context. Reasoning develops the asymmetric effects and long-term contribution to Soviet collapse. CER fully integrated.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim about détente and Helsinki. Two specific evidence points. Reasoning addresses either the short-term achievement or the long-term effect but not both fully.
2 - Developing: General claim about détente being a period of reduced tension. One specific evidence point. Reasoning is mostly narrative.
1 - Beginning: Vague claim. Minimal evidence. No analytical reasoning.
0 - No response or off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Helsinki 'three baskets' structure; Helsinki Watch Groups (1976–1977); Solidarity movement in Poland (1980–1981); Charter 77 (Czechoslovakia, 1977); SALT I (1972) and SALT II (1979); Nixon-Brezhnev summits; INF Treaty (1987); connection to Gorbachev's glasnost/perestroika as the Helsinki framework's ultimate expression.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: La afirmación identifica la naturaleza de doble filo de Helsinki. La evidencia incluye al menos tres detalles específicos. El razonamiento desarrolla los efectos asimétricos y la contribución a largo plazo al colapso soviético.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara sobre la distensión y Helsinki. Dos puntos de evidencia específica.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación general sobre la distensión como un período de tensión reducida. Un punto de evidencia específica.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga. Evidencia mínima.
0 - Sin respuesta o fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Estructura de las 'tres cestas' de Helsinki; Grupos Helsinki Watch (1976–1977); movimiento Solidaridad en Polonia (1980–1981); Carta 77 (Checoslovaquia, 1977); SALT I (1972) y SALT II (1979); Tratado INF (1987).

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President Ronald Reagan's Address to the British Parliament (Westminster Address), June 8, 1982 — a U.S. government document available through the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library (National Archives):

"What I am describing now is a plan and a hope for the long term — the march of freedom and democracy which will leave Marxism-Leninism on the ash heap of history as it has left other tyrannies which stifle the freedom and muzzle the self-expression of the people. And that's why we must continue our efforts to strengthen NATO even as we move forward with our zero-option proposal in the negotiations on intermediate-range forces and our proposal for a one-third reduction in strategic ballistic missile warheads."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of Reagan's Cold War strategy (US.69), write a CER response that analyzes how Reagan's approach to ending the Cold War combined ideological confrontation with strategic negotiation. Your response must evaluate whether the end of the Cold War was primarily a result of Reagan's policies, internal Soviet contradictions, or a combination of both, drawing on evidence from the full arc of Cold War competition (US.59–US.70).
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del Discurso del Presidente Ronald Reagan ante el Parlamento Británico (Discurso de Westminster), 8 de junio de 1982 — un documento del gobierno de EE. UU. disponible a través de la Biblioteca Presidencial Ronald Reagan (Archivos Nacionales):

"Lo que estoy describiendo ahora es un plan y una esperanza a largo plazo: la marcha de la libertad y la democracia que dejará al marxismo-leninismo en el basurero de la historia, tal como ha dejado otras tiranías que sofocan la libertad y silencian la autoexpresión del pueblo."

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la estrategia de Reagan durante la Guerra Fría (US.69), escribe una respuesta CER que analice cómo el enfoque de Reagan para poner fin a la Guerra Fría combinó la confrontación ideológica con la negociación estratégica.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — The end of the Cold War resulted from the convergence of Reagan's deliberate pressure strategy with the internal structural collapse of Soviet communism, with neither cause sufficient alone — Reagan exploited pre-existing Soviet vulnerabilities that decades of Cold War competition had created, but the fundamental cause was the failure of the Soviet economic and political system. EVIDENCE — (1) Reagan's 'peace through strength' buildup: defense spending increase from $171 billion (1981) to $376 billion (1986); (2) Reagan Doctrine — support for anti-communist insurgencies in Afghanistan (mujahideen), Nicaragua (Contras), Angola, and elsewhere; (3) SDI (Strategic Defense Initiative, 1983) — whether viable or not, it forced Soviet responses that strained their economy; (4) INF Treaty (1987) — Reagan negotiated with Gorbachev despite his own confrontational rhetoric, showing the dual-track approach; (5) Gorbachev's glasnost and perestroika (1985–1991) as recognition of systemic Soviet failure that pre-dated Reagan's presidency; (6) Soviet overextension: Afghan war costs (1979–1989), satellite state subsidies, technological gap. REASONING — Reagan's Westminster address excerpt reveals the ideological dimension — 'ash heap of history' echoes Trotsky and signals Reagan's belief that history's trajectory favored democracy. But the student should reason that this ideological confidence was matched by pragmatic negotiation (INF Treaty) and that Soviet collapse was ultimately driven by internal factors (economic stagnation, nationalism in Soviet republics, Chernobyl's legitimacy crisis) that Reagan's pressure accelerated but did not create.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.69, US.70 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Claim identifies the multi-causal explanation (Reagan pressure + Soviet internal collapse). Evidence spans both Reagan's specific policies and Soviet internal factors, with at least three specific details. Reasoning synthesizes across the full Cold War arc (US.59–US.70), connecting the origins of Soviet overextension to its final collapse. CER fully integrated.
3 - Proficient: Clear multi-causal or evaluative claim. Two specific evidence points. Reasoning addresses both Reagan policies and Soviet factors but may not synthesize across the full Cold War arc.
2 - Developing: Claim attributes the end primarily to Reagan or primarily to Soviet collapse without nuance. One specific evidence point. Reasoning is mostly narrative.
1 - Beginning: Vague claim. Minimal evidence. No analytical reasoning.
0 - No response or off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Reagan defense buildup (budget figures); Reagan Doctrine (Afghanistan, Nicaragua); SDI announcement (1983); INF Treaty (1987); Gorbachev's glasnost and perestroika (1985–1991); Soviet Afghan War (1979–1989); Chernobyl disaster (1986) as legitimacy crisis; fall of Berlin Wall (Nov. 1989, US.70); dissolution of USSR (Dec. 1991).
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: La afirmación identifica la explicación multicausal (presión de Reagan + colapso interno soviético). La evidencia abarca tanto las políticas específicas de Reagan como los factores internos soviéticos. El razonamiento sintetiza a lo largo de todo el arco de la Guerra Fría.
3 - Competente: Afirmación multicausal o evaluativa clara. Dos puntos de evidencia específica.
2 - En desarrollo: La afirmación atribuye el fin principalmente a Reagan o principalmente al colapso soviético sin matices. Un punto de evidencia específica.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga. Evidencia mínima.
0 - Sin respuesta o fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Reconstrucción de defensa de Reagan (cifras presupuestarias); Doctrina Reagan (Afganistán, Nicaragua); anuncio de la SDI (1983); Tratado INF (1987); glasnost y perestroika de Gorbachev (1985–1991); Guerra de Afganistán soviética (1979–1989); caída del Muro de Berlín (noviembre de 1989).

items.stem:
DOCUMENT-BASED QUESTION: The Fall of the Berlin Wall and the Collapse of the Soviet Union

Directions: Read the following two primary source excerpts and respond to the prompt below. Apply HIPP analysis to both documents and construct an argument.

---
DOCUMENT A: Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev, Speech to the United Nations General Assembly, December 7, 1988 — United Nations official record:
"The use of force no longer can or must be an instrument of foreign policy. This applies above all to nuclear arms, but that is not the only thing that matters. All of us — and I want to say this with the utmost conviction — all of us must act in a new way, think in a new way. The de-ideologization of interstate relations has become a demand of the new times. We intend to live up to that demand."

DOCUMENT B: President George H.W. Bush, Address to the Nation on the End of the Cold War, December 25, 1991 — U.S. government document, available through the George H.W. Bush Presidential Library (National Archives):
"At Christmas time, we remember how many people — in Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, in all the former Soviet republics — had lived under the shadow of repression. Today, for the most part, that shadow has been lifted... This is a victory for democracy and freedom. It's a victory for the moral force of our values. Every American can take pride in this victory."

---
Using both documents and your knowledge of the end of the Cold War (US.70, US.59–US.69), construct an argument that evaluates the relative contributions of American Cold War strategy and Soviet internal reform to the Cold War's conclusion. Apply HIPP analysis to both documents and address: (1) what Gorbachev's 1988 UN speech reveals about the fundamental shift in Soviet foreign policy thinking that made the peaceful end of the Cold War possible; (2) whether Bush's framing of the Cold War's end as an American 'victory' is historically accurate or oversimplified; and (3) how the end of the Cold War connects to and validates (or complicates) the containment strategy that originated with Kennan in 1946 (US.59–US.60).
items.stemEs:
PREGUNTA BASADA EN DOCUMENTOS: La Caída del Muro de Berlín y el Colapso de la Unión Soviética

Instrucciones: Lee los siguientes dos fragmentos de fuentes primarias y responde al indicador. Aplica el análisis HIPP a ambos documentos.

DOCUMENTO A: Secretario General Soviético Mikhail Gorbachev, Discurso ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas, 7 de diciembre de 1988.
"El uso de la fuerza ya no puede ni debe ser un instrumento de política exterior... La des-ideologización de las relaciones interestatales se ha convertido en una demanda de los nuevos tiempos."

DOCUMENTO B: Presidente George H.W. Bush, Discurso a la Nación sobre el Fin de la Guerra Fría, 25 de diciembre de 1991.
"Esta es una victoria para la democracia y la libertad. Es una victoria para la fuerza moral de nuestros valores."

Usando ambos documentos y tu conocimiento del fin de la Guerra Fría (US.70, US.59–US.69), construye un argumento que evalúe las contribuciones relativas de la estrategia de EE. UU. en la Guerra Fría y la reforma interna soviética a la conclusión de la Guerra Fría.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (6/6) response would include: THESIS — A precise, arguable thesis that addresses the multi-causal question of the Cold War's end (e.g., 'The peaceful end of the Cold War resulted primarily from Gorbachev's recognition that the Soviet system's internal contradictions required fundamental reform — a reform that dismantled the ideological and military competition that the West's containment strategy had sustained but not resolved — making the end a Soviet-initiated transformation that American pressure had created conditions for but could not have compelled'). HIPP ANALYSIS: Document A — Historical context: Gorbachev speaks 14 months after the INF Treaty, 3 years into glasnost/perestroika, as Soviet finances are strained by Afghan war and the arms race; Intended audience: UN General Assembly and global leadership, but clearly directed at Western governments and their publics; Purpose: To signal a fundamental shift in Soviet foreign policy — the renunciation of the Brezhnev Doctrine and implicit acknowledgment that Eastern European states could choose their own paths; Point of view: Gorbachev's 'de-ideologization' language is a direct repudiation of the Soviet ideological framework that had justified Cold War confrontation — he is essentially announcing the end of the ideological competition by renouncing Soviet universalism. Document B — Historical context: Bush speaks on Christmas Day, the day Gorbachev resigned and the Soviet flag was lowered — he is giving a retrospective framing of an event he did not predict (U.S. intelligence did not forecast Soviet collapse by 1991); Intended audience: American public; Purpose: To provide a satisfying narrative of Cold War victory that validates decades of defense spending and sacrifice; Point of view: Bush's 'victory' framing is politically useful but historically incomplete — it obscures the role of Soviet internal reforms (not American pressure alone) and the danger of triumphalism that would shape post-Cold War U.S. foreign policy. OUTSIDE EVIDENCE: Brezhnev Doctrine (1968) and its repudiation; revolutions of 1989 (Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, East Germany, Romania); Berlin Wall fall (Nov. 9, 1989); German reunification (Oct. 3, 1990); dissolution of USSR (Dec. 25, 1991) and 15 successor republics; Kennan's original prediction that patient containment would 'mellow' Soviet behavior — a 45-year vindication.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.70, US.59 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Precise, arguable thesis addressing the multi-causal explanation that avoids simple 'American victory' framing. Full HIPP on both documents (all four elements, with historical accuracy including Gorbachev's UN speech as Brezhnev Doctrine repudiation and Bush's framing limitations). Outside evidence (minimum 3 specific facts spanning the full Cold War arc). Addresses all three prompt components. Synthesis connects back to Kennan and containment's original logic — the ultimate validation of patience.
5 - Advanced: Clear thesis addressing multi-causation. Full HIPP on both documents. Two outside evidence points. Addresses two of three prompt components.
4 - Proficient: Arguable thesis. HIPP partially applied to both documents. One outside evidence fact. Addresses two prompt components.
3 - Adequate: General thesis. Analyzes both documents without systematic HIPP. Some outside knowledge.
2 - Developing: Basic claim. References documents, mostly summary.
1 - Beginning: Attempts a response without substantive analysis.
0 - No response or off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Document A HIPP — Gorbachev's 'de-ideologization' as direct Brezhnev Doctrine repudiation; UN audience as deliberate signal to Eastern European satellites; 'new way of thinking' as acknowledgment of Soviet system failure. Document B HIPP — Bush's 'victory' framing as politically convenient narrative; the limitation of the 'moral force' argument given U.S. Cold War alliances with authoritarian states; Bush's deliberate restraint in not gloating at the actual moment of Soviet collapse.
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Brezhnev Doctrine (1968) and its implicit revocation by Document A; East European revolutions of 1989; Solidarity's electoral victory (Poland, June 1989); Hungarian border opening (May 1989); Berlin Wall fall (Nov. 9, 1989); German reunification (Oct. 3, 1990); Baltic independence declarations; Soviet dissolution (Dec. 25, 1991); Kennan's 1947 prediction of Soviet mellowing as 45-year vindication.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: Tesis precisa y argumentable que aborda la explicación multicausal que evita el simple encuadre de 'victoria americana'. HIPP completo en ambos documentos. Evidencia externa (mínimo 3 hechos específicos que abarcan todo el arco de la Guerra Fría). Aborda los tres componentes del indicador.
5 - Avanzado: Tesis clara que aborda la multicausalidad. HIPP completo en ambos documentos. Dos puntos de evidencia externa.
4 - Competente: Tesis argumentable. HIPP parcialmente aplicado. Un hecho de evidencia externa específica.
3 - Adecuado: Tesis general. Analiza ambos documentos sin HIPP sistemático. Algún conocimiento externo.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación básica. Referencias a documentos, principalmente resumen.
1 - Inicial: Intenta una respuesta sin análisis sustantivo.
0 - Sin respuesta o fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Doctrina Brezhnev (1968) y su revocación implícita; revoluciones de Europa del Este de 1989; caída del Muro de Berlín (9 de nov. de 1989); reunificación alemana (3 de oct. de 1990); disolución soviética (25 de dic. de 1991); predicción de Kennan de 1947 como vindicación de 45 años.

items.stem:
Extended Response — No sources provided. Draw on your knowledge of Cold War history (US.59–US.70).

The Space Race (1957–1969) is often treated as a scientific competition, but historians argue it was fundamentally a Cold War ideological contest with profound domestic and international consequences. Using the CER framework, write an extended response that evaluates this claim. Your response should: (1) construct a thesis about the Space Race's primary significance — was it scientific achievement, military competition, ideological demonstration, or some combination?; (2) analyze at least four specific Space Race milestones or policy decisions and explain their Cold War significance; and (3) assess whether the Space Race ultimately served American strategic interests effectively, drawing on evidence across US.65, US.67, and the broader Cold War context (US.59–US.70).
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida — No se proporcionan fuentes. Basa tu respuesta en tu conocimiento de la historia de la Guerra Fría (US.59–US.70).

La Carrera Espacial (1957–1969) a menudo se trata como una competencia científica, pero los historiadores argumentan que fue fundamentalmente una contienda ideológica de la Guerra Fría con profundas consecuencias domésticas e internacionales. Usando el marco CER, escribe una respuesta extendida que evalúe esta afirmación. Tu respuesta debe: (1) construir una tesis sobre la importancia primaria de la Carrera Espacial; (2) analizar al menos cuatro hitos específicos de la Carrera Espacial o decisiones políticas; y (3) evaluar si la Carrera Espacial sirvió efectivamente a los intereses estratégicos estadounidenses.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) extended response would include: CLAIM — A precise, defensible thesis (e.g., 'The Space Race was simultaneously an ideological demonstration, a military competition, and a domestic mobilization project, but its primary Cold War significance was as an ideological contest: each milestone was designed to prove systemic superiority to both domestic and global audiences, making the Moon landing the Cold War's most effective single act of political communication'). EVIDENCE across four milestones/decisions: (1) Sputnik (Oct. 4, 1957) — demonstrated Soviet ICBM-range rocket capability, triggering the National Defense Education Act (1958) as a domestic educational mobilization and NASA's creation as an institutional response; (2) Yuri Gagarin's orbit (April 12, 1961) — coming 4 days before the Bay of Pigs, it created maximum political pressure on Kennedy and directly produced the Moon commitment; (3) Apollo 1 fire (January 27, 1967) — 3 American astronauts killed, testing the nation's commitment; Soviets' parallel N1 rocket failures kept secret, demonstrating the asymmetric transparency of democratic vs. totalitarian systems; (4) Apollo 11 Moon landing (July 20, 1969) — global television audience of 600 million; 'one small step' as the Space Race's ideological payoff; simultaneous demonstration of American technological and economic capability. REASONING — The student should reason that the Space Race's military dimension (ICBM development, reconnaissance satellites) was real but secondary to its ideological function: both superpowers understood that space achievement signaled systemic capability to the non-aligned world. The Moon landing effectively 'won' the ideological competition by demonstrating American technological superiority at the exact moment the Vietnam War was undermining American credibility. SYNTHESIS — The student should connect the Space Race's military-industrial complex costs (US.67) to Eisenhower's warning, and assess whether the $25 billion Apollo investment was an efficient Cold War expenditure relative to its ideological payoff.

Détente — the policy of relaxing Cold War tensions pursued by Nixon, Ford, and Carter — represented a fundamental shift in U.S. Cold War strategy from ideological confrontation to pragmatic accommodation. Yet détente failed to achieve lasting stability and was effectively abandoned by the Reagan administration. Using the CER framework, write an extended response that evaluates détente as a Cold War strategy. Your response should: (1) construct a thesis about whether détente was a strategic success, failure, or something more complex; (2) analyze at least four specific détente achievements or failures using specific historical evidence; and (3) evaluate why détente ultimately gave way to Reagan's confrontational approach and assess which strategy was more effective in contributing to the Cold War's end, synthesizing knowledge across US.66, US.68, US.69, and US.70.
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida — No se proporcionan fuentes. Basa tu respuesta en tu conocimiento de la historia de la Guerra Fría (US.59–US.70).

La distensión — la política de relajar las tensiones de la Guerra Fría perseguida por Nixon, Ford y Carter — representó un cambio fundamental en la estrategia de EE. UU. en la Guerra Fría, pasando de la confrontación ideológica a la acomodación pragmática. Sin embargo, la distensión no logró una estabilidad duradera y fue efectivamente abandonada por la administración Reagan. Usando el marco CER, escribe una respuesta extendida que evalúe la distensión como una estrategia de Guerra Fría. Tu respuesta debe: (1) construir una tesis sobre si la distensión fue un éxito estratégico, un fracaso o algo más complejo; (2) analizar al menos cuatro logros o fracasos específicos de la distensión; y (3) evaluar por qué la distensión finalmente cedió paso al enfoque confrontacional de Reagan.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) extended response would include: CLAIM — A precise, defensible thesis that addresses détente's complex legacy (e.g., 'Détente was a strategically sophisticated recognition of Cold War realities — nuclear parity, Soviet regional power, and American overextension after Vietnam — that achieved real arms control and crisis management goals, but ultimately failed as a grand strategy because it could not resolve the fundamental incompatibility of Soviet and American interests, a failure Reagan's strategy exposed by exploiting Soviet economic and political vulnerabilities that détente had stabilized rather than addressed'). EVIDENCE across four achievements/failures: (1) SALT I (1972) and ABM Treaty — capped strategic nuclear weapons for the first time; created the framework for arms reduction that continued through Reagan's INF Treaty; genuine achievement in reducing nuclear risk; (2) Nixon-Brezhnev summits and triangular diplomacy (China opening, 1972) — used China as leverage against Soviet Union, a sophisticated realist achievement; (3) Helsinki Accords (1975) — recognized Soviet borders but embedded human rights provisions that became long-term Soviet liabilities (Helsinki Watch Groups, Solidarity, Charter 77); (4) Détente's failures: Soviet adventurism in Angola (1975), Ethiopia (1977–78), and Afghanistan (1979) despite détente — showed that détente constrained U.S. response more than Soviet action; Soviet invasion of Afghanistan (December 1979) effectively killed détente under Carter; SALT II (1979) — signed but never ratified, showing détente's domestic political limits. REASONING — The student should reason that détente's failure was not simply because Reagan was right and Carter/Ford were wrong, but because détente attempted to manage an ideological competition through diplomatic instruments without addressing the systemic contradictions that made Soviet expansion and U.S. resistance structurally necessary. Reagan's confrontational approach worked partly because Gorbachev was both willing and able to reform — détente had not forced Soviet internal change, it had merely moderated its external expression. SYNTHESIS — The student should synthesize US.66 (Cuban Missile Crisis as the moment nuclear parity was acknowledged and created détente's precondition), US.68 (détente's specific mechanisms), US.69 (Reagan's abandonment and escalation), and US.70 (the end proving that internal Soviet collapse, not American pressure alone, determined the outcome).

4 - Exemplary: Precise, defensible thesis addressing the complex legacy question (not simply 'détente failed' or 'détente succeeded'). Analyzes at least four specific achievements/failures with accurate historical detail. Reasoning develops why détente was inadequate as a grand strategy without being simply wrong, and explains the relationship between détente and Reagan's approach. Synthesis spans US.66–US.70 and connects détente to the Cold War's end.
3 - Proficient: Clear thesis on détente's complexity. Analyzes three or four achievements/failures. Reasoning makes the strategic limitation argument but may not connect détente to the Cold War's end.
2 - Developing: General thesis about détente reducing tensions. Analyzes two achievements/failures. Reasoning is mostly descriptive.
1 - Beginning: Vague thesis. One element analyzed. Minimal reasoning.
0 - No response or off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Nixon's China opening (February 1972); SALT I (May 1972) and ABM Treaty; Nixon-Brezhnev Moscow Summit (1972); Watergate's effect on détente implementation; Ford-Brezhnev Vladivostok Summit (1974); Helsinki Accords (August 1975); Helsinki Watch Groups (1976–1977); Soviet Angola operation (1975); SALT II (June 1979) — signed but unratified; Soviet invasion of Afghanistan (December 1979) — détente's death blow; Carter Doctrine (January 1980); Reagan's 'evil empire' speech (1983) as détente's explicit repudiation; INF Treaty (1987) as the successor arms control achievement that détente made possible.
SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: The response should synthesize the Cuban Missile Crisis (US.66) as creating nuclear parity recognition → détente (US.68) → Reagan confrontation (US.69) → Soviet collapse (US.70), showing each phase built on the contradictions of its predecessor.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Tesis precisa y defendible que aborda la pregunta sobre el legado complejo. Analiza al menos cuatro logros/fracasos específicos. El razonamiento desarrolla por qué la distensión fue inadecuada como gran estrategia sin ser simplemente errónea.

2 - En desarrollo: Tesis general sobre la reducción de tensiones por la distensión. Analiza dos logros/fracasos.

EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: La respuesta debe sintetizar la Crisis de los Misiles Cubanos (US.66) como creadora del reconocimiento de paridad nuclear → distensión (US.68) → confrontación Reagan (US.69) → colapso soviético (US.70).

The Cold War ended peacefully in 1989–1991 — a remarkable outcome given that for decades the conflict seemed capable of producing nuclear catastrophe. Historians debate whether this outcome was the result of American Cold War strategy, Soviet internal failure, the agency of individuals like Gorbachev, or structural forces that made Soviet collapse inevitable. Using the CER framework, write an extended response that constructs and defends a comprehensive explanation for why the Cold War ended when it did, how it did. Your response should: (1) construct a thesis that identifies the most significant causal factor(s) in the Cold War's peaceful conclusion; (2) analyze at least five specific factors — including at minimum one American policy factor, one Soviet internal factor, one structural/economic factor, and one individual agency factor — with specific historical evidence for each; and (3) evaluate the long-term significance of the Cold War's outcome for American foreign policy and global order, synthesizing knowledge across the full arc of the Cold War (US.59–US.70).
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida — No se proporcionan fuentes. Basa tu respuesta en tu conocimiento de la historia de la Guerra Fría (US.59–US.70).

La Guerra Fría terminó pacíficamente en 1989–1991 — un resultado notable dado que durante décadas el conflicto pareció capaz de producir una catástrofe nuclear. Los historiadores debaten si este resultado fue el resultado de la estrategia de EE. UU. en la Guerra Fría, el fracaso interno soviético, la agencia de individuos como Gorbachev, o fuerzas estructurales que hicieron inevitable el colapso soviético. Usando el marco CER, escribe una respuesta extendida que construya y defienda una explicación comprensiva de por qué la Guerra Fría terminó cuando lo hizo y cómo lo hizo. Tu respuesta debe: (1) construir una tesis que identifique el/los factor(es) causal(es) más significativo(s); (2) analizar al menos cinco factores específicos; y (3) evaluar la importancia a largo plazo del resultado de la Guerra Fría.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) extended response would include: CLAIM — A sophisticated, defensible thesis that integrates multiple causal factors (e.g., 'The Cold War's peaceful conclusion resulted from the convergence of American sustained pressure, Soviet structural economic failure, and the transformative agency of Gorbachev — but the peace itself, as distinct from Soviet collapse, was not inevitable: it required Gorbachev's personal decision to renounce the Brezhnev Doctrine and Reagan's willingness to negotiate, demonstrating that structural forces created the conditions but individual choices determined the outcome'). EVIDENCE across five factors (minimum): American Policy Factor — Reagan's 'peace through strength' (defense buildup forcing Soviet expenditure), Reagan Doctrine support for anti-communist insurgencies, SDI psychological pressure, INF Treaty (1987) showing dual-track strategy; Soviet Internal Factor — Soviet economic stagnation: GDP growth of ~2% annually through 1980s vs. U.S. ~4%; technological gap in civilian economy; Afghan War costs ($50 billion over 10 years, 15,000 Soviet soldiers killed); structural agricultural failure; Structural/Economic Factor — The fundamental economic incompatibility of Soviet central planning with the technological demands of late-20th-century global competition: the information economy that drove U.S. productivity growth (personal computers, internet precursors) was structurally incompatible with Soviet political controls; Individual Agency Factor — Gorbachev's specific decisions: glasnost, perestroika, Sinatra Doctrine (Eastern European states free to choose), refusal to use military force in 1989 revolutions (unlike 1956 Hungary and 1968 Czechoslovakia); fifth factor optional: Eastern European peoples' agency — Solidarity in Poland, Civic Forum in Czechoslovakia, Leipzig demonstrations in East Germany. REASONING — The student should reason through the counterfactual: if Gorbachev had been replaced by a hardliner in 1985 (as was possible given Soviet leadership succession patterns), would the structural pressures alone have produced a peaceful end? The answer is uncertain — Tiananmen Square (1989) showed another response to pressure was possible. The Cold War ended peacefully because structural forces created the conditions AND specific individuals made specific choices consistent with peaceful resolution. SYNTHESIS — The response must span the full arc: Kennan's 1947 prediction of Soviet 'mellowing' (US.59–US.60) → 45 years of containment → Cuban Missile Crisis near-catastrophe (US.66) → détente's managed competition (US.68) → Reagan's escalation (US.69) → Gorbachev's reform → peaceful end (US.70) — showing that containment's logic was ultimately vindicated but through a path no one predicted.

Analyzes at least five specific factors with historical accuracy, including all required types (American policy, Soviet internal, structural/economic, individual agency). Reasoning develops the counterfactual (what if no Gorbachev?) to test causal claims. Synthesis spans the full Cold War arc (US.59–US.70) and connects to post-Cold War foreign policy implications.

2 - Developing: General thesis (e.g., 'the Soviet Union collapsed because of its own problems'). Analyzes three factors. Reasoning is mostly descriptive rather than analytical. Limited synthesis.
1 - Beginning: Vague thesis. Two factors mentioned. Minimal reasoning. No synthesis.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Reagan defense buildup (1981–1986 budget figures); Reagan Doctrine specifics; SDI (March 23, 1983); INF Treaty (Dec. 8, 1987); Soviet GDP growth rates (~2% vs. U.S. ~4%); Afghan War (Dec. 1979–Feb. 1989, approximately 14,000 Soviet deaths, $50 billion); Chernobyl (April 26, 1986) as legitimacy crisis; Gorbachev's glasnost (introduced 1986) and perestroika (introduced 1986; book 1987); Sinatra Doctrine (Oct. 1989); Polish Solidarity electoral victory (June 1989); Hungarian border opening (May 1989); Leipzig Monday demonstrations; Berlin Wall fall (Nov. 9, 1989); German reunification (Oct. 3, 1990); Baltic independence; Soviet coup attempt (Aug. 19–22, 1991); Gorbachev resignation and Soviet dissolution (Dec. 25, 1991).
SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: The response must connect Kennan's original 1947 prediction of Soviet 'mellowing' to the 1991 outcome, showing whether containment 'worked' as Kennan intended or produced a different ending than he anticipated. The post-Cold War implication: U.S. unipolarity (1991–2000s) and the 'unipolar moment' as the Cold War's immediate legacy.

4 - Ejemplar: Tesis sofisticada y defendible que integra múltiples factores causales. Analiza al menos cinco factores específicos con precisión histórica, incluyendo todos los tipos requeridos. El razonamiento desarrolla el contrafactual. La síntesis abarca todo el arco de la Guerra Fría (US.59–US.70).

UU.); Guerra de Afganistán; Chernobyl (26 de abril de 1986); glasnost (introducida 1986) y perestroika (introducida 1986; libro 1987) de Gorbachev; Doctrina Sinatra (oct. 1989); caída del Muro de Berlín (9 de nov. de 1989); reunificación alemana (3 de oct. de 1990); disolución soviética (25 de dic. de 1991).
EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: La respuesta debe conectar la predicción original de Kennan de 1947 del 'ablandamiento' soviético con el resultado de 1991, mostrando si la contención 'funcionó' como Kennan pretendía.

items.stem:
DOCUMENT-BASED QUESTION: Reagan and the End of the Cold War

Directions: Read the following two primary source excerpts and respond to the prompt below. Apply SOAPS analysis to both documents and construct an argument.

---
DOCUMENT A: President Ronald Reagan, "Tear Down This Wall" speech, Brandenburg Gate, West Berlin, June 12, 1987 — U.S. government document, available through the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library (National Archives):
"General Secretary Gorbachev, if you seek peace, if you seek prosperity for the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, if you seek liberalization: Come here to this gate! Mr. Gorbachev, open this gate! Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!... We hear much from Moscow about a new policy of reform and openness. Some political prisoners have been released. Certain foreign news broadcasts are no longer being jammed. Some economic enterprises have been permitted to operate with greater freedom from state control. Are these the beginnings of profound changes in the Soviet state? Or are these token gestures, intended to raise false hopes in the West?"

DOCUMENT B: President Ronald Reagan, Address to the Nation on the Iran-Contra Affair, March 4, 1987 — U.S. government document, available through the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library (National Archives):
"A few months ago I told the American people I did not trade arms for hostages. My heart and my best intentions still tell me that's true, but the facts and the evidence tell me it is not. As the Tower board reported, what began as a strategic opening to Iran deteriorated, in its implementation, into trading arms for hostages."

---
Using both documents and your knowledge of Reagan's Cold War strategy (US.69, US.70), construct an argument that evaluates the tensions and contradictions within Reagan's approach to ending the Cold War. Apply SOAPS analysis to both documents and address: (1) how the Berlin Wall speech reflects Reagan's ideological vision for Cold War resolution; (2) how the Iran-Contra scandal reveals the contradictions between Reagan's stated principles and actual foreign policy operations; and (3) whether Reagan's approach to the Cold War was primarily a coherent strategic vision or an improvised series of responses — and what evidence supports your evaluation.
items.stemEs:
PREGUNTA BASADA EN DOCUMENTOS: Reagan y el Fin de la Guerra Fría

Instrucciones: Lee los siguientes dos fragmentos de fuentes primarias y responde al indicador. Aplica el análisis SOAPS a ambos documentos.

DOCUMENTO A: Presidente Ronald Reagan, discurso "Derriba ese muro", Puerta de Brandeburgo, Berlín Occidental, 12 de junio de 1987.
"Secretario General Gorbachev, si busca la paz, si busca la prosperidad para la Unión Soviética y Europa del Este, si busca la liberalización: ¡Venga aquí a esta puerta! ¡Sr. Gorbachev, abra esta puerta! ¡Sr. Gorbachev, derriba este muro!"

DOCUMENTO B: Presidente Ronald Reagan, Discurso a la Nación sobre el Asunto Irán-Contra, 4 de marzo de 1987.
"Hace unos meses le dije al pueblo americano que no intercambié armas por rehenes. Mi corazón y mis mejores intenciones todavía me dicen que eso es cierto, pero los hechos y la evidencia me dicen que no lo es."

Usando ambos documentos y tu conocimiento de la estrategia de Reagan en la Guerra Fría (US.69, US.70), construye un argumento que evalúe las tensiones y contradicciones dentro del enfoque de Reagan para poner fin a la Guerra Fría.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (6/6) response would include: THESIS — A precise, arguable thesis (e.g., 'Reagan's Cold War strategy was defined by a genuine ideological vision of democratic triumph over communism that coexisted uneasily with covert operations and policy contradictions that undermined the moral authority he claimed — demonstrating that the Cold War's end required both Reagan's ideological pressure and Gorbachev's internal reforms, not Reagan's vision alone'). SOAPS ANALYSIS: Document A — Speaker: Reagan at the peak of his standing as Cold War ideological champion, addressing Gorbachev directly; Occasion: 26th anniversary of Berlin Wall's construction, Gorbachev's glasnost/perestroika ongoing; Audience: West Berliners, but the address was globally broadcast and directed at Gorbachev and Soviet leadership; Purpose: To challenge Gorbachev to prove glasnost was genuine by taking the symbolic action of opening the Wall — a rhetorical gambit that made the Wall's continued existence an ongoing propaganda liability for Moscow; Significance: Reagan's direct challenge was initially dismissed by State Dept. and NSC staff as too provocative — his insistence on keeping it reveals the personal ideological conviction behind his Cold War strategy. Document B — Speaker: Reagan in political crisis, 3 months after the Iran-Contra story broke; Occasion: National address following the Tower Commission Report confirming arms-for-hostages exchange; Audience: American public and Congress threatening impeachment; Purpose: To acknowledge limited wrongdoing while preserving his presidency and personal credibility; Significance: The contradiction between Reagan's stated principle (no negotiations with terrorists, no arms for hostages) and the operational reality reveals the gap between the Cold War's ideological framing and its actual execution — the Reagan Doctrine's covert operations often contradicted the democratic values Reagan championed. OUTSIDE EVIDENCE: Reagan Doctrine's specific operations (Afghanistan, Nicaragua, Angola); Iran-Contra specifics (Oliver North, NSC operations, Boland Amendment); INF Treaty signed Dec. 1987, same year as both documents — showing Reagan simultaneously advancing arms control; Berlin Wall fall (Nov. 9, 1989) — 28 months after the 'tear down this wall' speech.

choices.text: International immigration, particularly from Latin America and Southeast Asia
choices.textEs: International inmigración, particularly from Latin America and Southeast Asia

choices.text: In-migration from other states attracted by lower taxes, cost of living, and economic opportunities
choices.textEs: In-migration from other states attracted by lower taxes, cost of living, and economic opportunities

choices.text: The relocation of federal government agencies to Tennessee to reduce Washington D.C. congestion
choices.textEs: The relocation of gobierno federal agencies to Tennessee to reduce Washington D.C. congestion

choices.text: High birth rates among Tennessee's existing resident population
choices.textEs: High birth rates among Tennessee's existing population

items.explanation: Tennessee's recent population growth has been driven largely by people moving in from other states for jobs, lower taxes, and a cheaper cost of living. D is wrong because natural increase was not the main factor, and A is wrong because international immigration alone does not explain the trend. The pattern fits a larger movement of Americans toward fast-growing Sun Belt states.

items.stem: The 2008 housing bubble was sustained in part by 'securitization' — the practice of —
items.stemEs: The 2008 housing bubble was sustained in part by 'securitization' — the practice of:

choices.text: Mortgage companies selling their loans immediately after origination, eliminating their incentive to verify borrower quality
choices.textEs: Mortgage companies selling their loans immediately after origination, eliminating their incentive to verify borrower quality

choices.text: Using hedge funds to bet against mortgage-backed securities while simultaneously selling them
choices.textEs: Using hedge funds to bet against mortgage-backed securities while simultaneously selling them

choices.text: Government guarantees for all mortgages originated by banks with federal charters
choices.textEs: Government guarantees for all mortgages originated by banks with federal charters

choices.text: Bundling mortgages into securities sold to investors, spreading — but not eliminating — the risk of default
choices.textEs: Bundling mortgages into securities sold to investors, spreading — but not eliminating — the risk of default

items.explanation: Securitization means bundling many mortgages together into securities and selling them to investors. A is tempting because lenders did often sell loans quickly, but D best names the actual financial practice. This system spread mortgage risk through the economy and helped turn housing trouble into a global crisis.

choices.textEs: Tennessee's warm climate attracting retirees from colder Northern states

items.stem: How did the automobile influence the growth of American suburbs in the 1950s?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo influyó el automóvil en el crecimiento de los suburbios estadounidenses en la década de 1950?

choices.text: Cars became too expensive for most families to purchase and maintain
choices.textEs: Los autos se volvieron demasiado caros para la mayoría de familias para comprar

choices.text: Cars allowed workers to live far from cities and commute to their jobs
choices.textEs: Los autos permitieron a trabajadores vivir lejos de ciudades y viajar a sus empleos

choices.text: Public transportation replaced automobiles in most suburban communities
choices.textEs: El transporte público reemplazó a los automóviles en la mayoría de suburbios

choices.text: Automobiles were only available to wealthy urban families in the 1950s
choices.textEs: Los automóviles solo estaban disponibles para familias urbanas adineradas

items.explanation: Cars helped suburbs grow because they let people live farther from downtown and still travel to work each day. C is wrong because most suburbs depended on automobiles more than public transportation, and D is wrong because cars became common middle-class purchases in the 1950s. Automobile commuting reshaped the geography of American life.
items.explanationEs: Los autos asequibles y las nuevas autopistas hicieron posible que las familias vivieran en suburbios y viajaran a trabajos en la ciudad. Esto transformó la geografía estadounidense, creando comunidades suburbanas extensas centradas en el transporte automotriz.

items.stem: How did advances in medicine during the 1950s improve American life?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo mejoraron los avances en medicina durante la década de 1950 la vida estadounidense?

choices.text: Antibiotics were discovered for the first time during the Korean War
choices.textEs: Los antibióticos fueron descubiertos por primera vez durante la Guerra de Corea

choices.text: The government banned all medical research to cut federal spending
choices.textEs: El gobierno prohibió toda investigación médica para recortar gastos federales

choices.text: Medical costs declined dramatically making healthcare free for everyone
choices.textEs: Los costos médicos disminuyeron dramáticamente haciendo la salud gratuita para todos

choices.text: Jonas Salk's polio vaccine eliminated a feared childhood disease
choices.textEs: La vacuna contra la polio de Jonas Salk eliminó una temida enfermedad infantil

items.explanation: Medical advances improved life most clearly when the polio vaccine made a once-feared childhood disease far less common. A is wrong because antibiotics had been discovered before the 1950s, and C is wrong because healthcare did not become free for everyone. The success of the vaccine fed postwar confidence in science and medicine.
items.explanationEs: Jonas Salk desarrolló la vacuna contra la polio en 1955, eliminando virtualmente una enfermedad que había paralizado a miles de niños anualmente. Este avance simbolizó el optimismo de la era y la fe en el progreso científico.

items.stem: How did the G.I. Bill transform post-war American society?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo transformó la Ley G.I. la sociedad estadounidense de posguerra?

choices.text: It provided veterans with education benefits, home loans, and job training
choices.textEs: Proporcionó a los veteranos beneficios educativos, préstamos para vivienda y capacitación laboral

choices.text: It expanded the middle class and shifted workers from factories to offices
choices.textEs: Requirió que todos los veteranos sirvieran cinco años adicionales en el ejército

choices.text: It symbolized the counterculture's ideals of peace, music, and communal spirit
choices.textEs: Solo proporcionó beneficios financieros a oficiales, no a soldados alistados

choices.text: Rising household incomes, mass consumption of goods, and rapid suburban growth
choices.textEs: Fue un aumento de impuestos a los veteranos para pagar la Guerra Fría

items.explanation: The G.I. Bill transformed postwar society by helping veterans pay for college, buy houses, and train for jobs. B is wrong because it describes one later result of economic change rather than the law itself. By widening access to education and homeownership, the law helped build the modern middle class.
items.explanationEs: La Ley G.I. (1944) ayudó a millones de veteranos de la Segunda Guerra Mundial a asistir a la universidad, comprar viviendas e iniciar negocios. Creó una clase media masiva y alimentó el crecimiento suburbano.

items.stem: Credit default swaps — a financial instrument at the center of the 2008 crisis — functioned as —
items.stemEs: Credit default swaps — a financial instrument at the center of the 2008 crisis — functioned as:

choices.text: A type of derivative that spread mortgage risk across global financial institutions
choices.textEs: A type of derivative that spread mortgage risk across global financial institutions

choices.text: A type of derivative that spread mortgage risk across global financial institutions exclusively
choices.textEs: A type of derivative that spread mortgage risk across global financial institutions exclusively

choices.text: Government-backed guarantees that prevented mortgage defaults from cascading into bank failures
choices.textEs: Government-backed guarantees that prevented mortgage defaults from cascading into bank failures

choices.text: A form of insurance allowing investors to bet against the success of mortgage-backed securities
choices.textEs: A form of insurance allowing investors to bet against the success of mortgage-backed securities

items.explanation: Credit default swaps worked like insurance contracts that let investors bet on whether mortgage-backed securities would fail. A is partly true because these derivatives spread risk across many firms, but D best explains what the instrument actually did. Their widespread use helped connect losses at banks and insurers throughout the global system.
items.explanationEs: Credit default swaps worked like insurance contracts that let investors bet on whether mortgage-backed securities would fail. A is partly true because these derivatives spread risk across many firms, but D best explains what the instrument actually did. items.stem: How did the automobile transform American business and culture in the 1950s?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo transformó el automóvil los negocios y la cultura estadounidense en la década de 1950?

choices.text: It reduced consumer spending because families saved money on transit
choices.textEs: Redujo el gasto del consumidor porque las familias ahorraron en transporte

choices.text: It eliminated the need for any new road construction across the nation
choices.textEs: Eliminó la necesidad de cualquier nueva construcción de carreteras en la nación

choices.text: It created fast food chains, motels, shopping centers, and drive-ins
choices.textEs: Creó cadenas de comida rápida, moteles, centros comerciales y autocinemas

choices.text: It primarily benefited the railroad industry by increasing train travel
choices.textEs: Benefició principalmente a la industria ferroviaria aumentando viajes en tren

items.explanation: Automobiles transformed business and culture by encouraging fast-food chains, motels, shopping centers, and drive-in theaters. A is wrong because cars increased consumer spending instead of reducing it, and D is wrong because they did not mainly revive railroad travel. A car-centered economy became a defining feature of 1950s America.
items.explanationEs: El automóvil creó industrias completamente nuevas: McDonald's y otras cadenas de comida rápida, Holiday Inn y moteles de carretera, centros comerciales suburbanos y autocinemas. La cultura del auto se volvió central para la identidad y el comercio estadounidense.

items.stem: How did the automobile reshape American culture in the 1950s?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo remodeló el automóvil la cultura estadounidense en los años 1950?

choices.text: It created drive-in restaurants, motels, shopping centers, and suburban sprawl
choices.textEs: Creó restaurantes con servicio al auto, moteles, centros comerciales y expansión suburbana

choices.text: Growth of roadside services such as motels, service stations, and fast-food chains
choices.textEs: La mayoría de los estadounidenses no podían pagar autos y dependían del transporte público

choices.text: Air pollution increased as vehicle ownership and highway travel expanded
choices.textEs: El automóvil no tuvo impacto cultural más allá de las necesidades básicas de transporte

choices.text: It supported suburban commuting and encouraged development farther from city centers
choices.textEs: La propiedad de autos estaba limitada a familias adineradas en grandes ciudades

items.explanation: The automobile reshaped 1950s culture by creating drive-ins, roadside businesses, motels, shopping centers, and sprawling suburbs. D is wrong because commuting is only one effect, and B names a business trend without capturing the full cultural change. Car ownership became a symbol of freedom and middle-class life in postwar America.
items.explanationEs: El automóvil transformó la cultura estadounidense: cines y restaurantes con servicio al auto, moteles a lo largo de las autopistas, centros comerciales suburbanos y estilos de vida de viajeros diarios surgieron.

choices.textEs: It supported suburban commuting and encouraged development farther from city centers

This shift helped suburban sprawl become a normal feature of postwar America.

choices.text: The bundling of risky mortgages into complex financial instruments (mortgage-backed securities) that hid the underlying risk

choices.text: Credit rating agencies giving high ratings to risky mortgage-backed securities
choices.textEs: Credit rating agencies giving high ratings to risky mortgage-backed securities

choices.textEs: Banks issuing mortgages to borrowers who could not afford them (subprime lending)

A, B, and D all describe practices that actually fed the bubble by hiding risk or encouraging bad loans. The question highlights how easy credit and weak oversight helped create the crash.

choices.textEs: The growing influence of corporate funding in mobilizing conservative grassroots organizations

choices.textEs: The natural tendency of political parties to moderate over time as they seek broader electoral coalitions

choices.text: How minority factions within parties can capture control through procedural manipulation
choices.textEs: How minority factions within parties can capture control through procedural manipulation

A is wrong because funding mattered, but the key historical point is how activists changed the Republican Party itself. This shift helped intensify polarization in Congress and national elections.

items.stem: How did the growth of suburbs affect American cities?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo afectó el crecimiento de los suburbios a las ciudades estadounidenses?

choices.text: Highway construction often displaced city neighborhoods while resources favored suburban expansion
choices.textEs: Las familias blancas se mudaron a los suburbios mientras las minorías eran a menudo excluidas, llevando al declive urbano

choices.text: White families moved to suburbs while minorities were often excluded, leading to urban decline
choices.textEs: Los suburbios y las ciudades crecieron por igual y prosperaron juntos

choices.text: It supported suburban commuting and encouraged development farther from city centers
choices.textEs: Los centros urbanos se volvieron más ricos ya que los suburbios atraían a residentes más pobres

choices.text: Growth of roadside services such as motels, service stations, and fast-food chains
choices.textEs: El crecimiento suburbano no tuvo efecto en las ciudades o demografía estadounidense

items.explanation: Suburban growth often hurt cities because many white middle-class families left, while minority families were frequently blocked from following them into the suburbs. C is wrong because it explains why suburbs expanded, not how cities were affected. This pattern contributed to urban poverty, segregation, and declining city tax bases.
items.explanationEs: La "fuga blanca" a los suburbios dejó a las ciudades con bases impositivas en declive y pobreza creciente. Prácticas discriminatorias como el redlining impidieron que las minorías compraran viviendas suburbanas.

items.stem: How did postwar transportation policy contribute to urban inequality?

choices.text: It supported suburban commuting and encouraged development farther from city centers
choices.textEs: It supported suburban commuting and encouraged development farther from city centers

choices.text: White families moved to suburbs while minorities were often excluded, leading to urban decline
choices.textEs: White families moved to suburbs while minorities were often excluded, leading to urban decline

choices.text: Highway construction often displaced city neighborhoods while resources favored suburban expansion
choices.textEs: Highway construction often displaced city neighborhoods while resources favored suburban expansion

choices.text: Communist governments needed to physically prevent citizens from leaving, revealing system failure
choices.textEs: Communist governments needed to physically prevent citizens from leaving, revealing system failure

items.explanation: Postwar transportation policy widened urban inequality because highway construction often cut through city neighborhoods while public investment favored suburban expansion. B is tempting because white flight was part of the result, but A best identifies the policy choice that caused the inequality. These decisions left many minority urban communities more isolated and underfunded.

B is tempting because white flight was part of the result, but A best identifies the policy choice that caused the inigualdad. These decisions left many minority urban communities more isolated and underfunded.

items.stem: How did advances in medicine and public health during the Eisenhower era affect American society?

choices.text: Medical advances had little impact because most Americans still relied on traditional home remedies rather than professional medical care
Developments such as the Salk polio vaccine reduced childhood disease mortality, improved average life expectancy, and increased public confidence in scientific medicine
Medical advances during the 1950s were limited to military hospitals and were not available to the general public until the 1970s
The Eisenhower administration nationalized all hospitals, making medical care universally free for American citizens

items.explanation: Jonas Salk's polio vaccine (1955) virtually eliminated a disease that had paralyzed thousands annually; antibiotics, improved surgical techniques, and hospital expansion also raised life expectancy and transformed public health.

items.stem: How did the widespread adoption of the automobile in the 1950s contribute to the growth of new types of businesses along American roads and highways?

choices.text: Automobile use declined in the 1950s as Americans preferred rail travel, limiting highway business development
Automobile use only affected business in rural areas, with no impact on suburban or urban commercial development
The car-owning population created demand for drive-in restaurants, roadside motels, gas stations, and drive-in theaters that clustered along highways and suburban roads
The government prohibited commercial development along highways to maintain road safety, limiting auto-oriented businesses

items.explanation: The automobile transformed commercial geography; McDonald's (1954), Holiday Inn (1952), and thousands of roadside businesses emerged to serve the mobile consumer, establishing the car-oriented commercial strip as a defining feature of American landscape.

items.stem: How did automobile ownership change where Americans chose to live during the 1950s?

choices.text: Cars caused Americans to move into city centers since parking was only available in dense urban areas
Car ownership caused most Americans to move to rural areas where gasoline was cheapest
Automobile ownership had little effect on residential patterns because most people still walked to work
Car ownership made it unnecessary to live near workplaces, allowing families to settle in suburbs while commuting to urban jobs

items.explanation: The car liberated families from proximity to workplaces; suburban developments like Levittown thrived because residents could commute by car to city jobs while enjoying larger homes and yards at lower cost.

items.stem: Which pattern best describes how automobile culture changed American eating habits during the 1950s?

choices.text: Drive-in restaurants and fast food chains offered quick, standardized, affordable meals to car-driving families, transforming American dining habits
The automobile had no effect on American diets because all food continued to be prepared at home throughout the 1950s
Car culture led Americans to eat exclusively at formal restaurants as a symbol of newfound affluence
Drive-in restaurants were only popular in rural communities and never achieved mainstream acceptance

items.explanation: Drive-in restaurants emerged as quintessential car-culture institutions; McDonald's Ray Kroc's franchise system (launched 1954) standardized fast, cheap automobile-oriented food service, transforming American eating habits permanently.

items.stem: How did the growth of automobile culture in the 1950s affect public transportation in American cities?

choices.text: Car culture strengthened urban public transit by increasing the number of people commuting into city centers
As automobile ownership spread and highway construction diverted public investment, many cities dismantled streetcar systems and cut transit funding
Cities expanded public transportation to compete with automobiles, resulting in larger and more efficient transit networks
Public transportation was unaffected because it served different passengers than those who owned automobiles

items.explanation: Declining ridership, highway competition for funding, and deliberate dismantling of streetcar systems (by automotive and oil interests) devastated urban transit; by 1970 most American cities had no functional streetcar networks.

items.stem: How did the motel industry's growth in the 1950s reflect changes in how Americans used the automobile?

choices.text: The motel industry declined in the 1950s as airplane travel became the preferred vacation method
Motels replaced hotels because the government required all lodging to be built adjacent to highways
Motels emerged because Americans began taking long-distance road trips for leisure, creating demand for affordable roadside lodging accessible by car
Motels were built exclusively for commercial truckers rather than for family leisure travel

items.explanation: Rising car ownership and vacation time enabled millions of families to take road trips; Holiday Inn (1952) and other chains standardized affordable roadside lodging, creating the modern motel industry as a direct product of automobile culture.

items.stem: How did the automobile industry's growth in the 1950s affect related sectors of the American economy?

choices.text: Auto industry growth was largely self-contained and had minimal impact on other economic sectors
The auto industry's growth caused a decline in suburban development because workers preferred to live near urban factories
The automobile industry reduced employment in manufacturing because assembly line automation eliminated more jobs than it created
The automobile industry stimulated demand in steel, rubber, petroleum, glass, and road construction, making it a central driver of the broader postwar economy

items.explanation: By the mid-1950s, one in six U.S. jobs was linked to automobiles; the industry drove demand across steel, rubber, oil, glass, and insurance sectors while high UAW wages enabled workers to participate in the consumer economy.
